We decided to give a baby a mat, and the other two nothing (we even gave my daughter the mat!) and even though my sons arent  throwers, MORE food ended up on the floor by them than by my daughter, this also means more food into their growing tummies! Its not as easy to roll up as it came, like another reviewer said its like a road-map, it never folds back the way you want it to (unless you fiddle with it for a few minutes) and if you roll it too tightly its shape will be curved and wont stick (not permanent damage, it will smooth out again, just not for that meal). We now just wrap an average sized rubberband around it twice, and it has the diameter of about a 50 cent coin. This means they are annoying to travel with (even more-so if you cant get it to roll up) and take up quite a bit of room in a diaperbag, rolled or not... but its all worth it. They can be easily washed in our double sink, or any sink I presume. They cant be easily wiped with a napkin, cloth, or wipe, but we just scrape the food off with a fork onto one of our plates, than just roll it up, and place it in a little bag (if we dont have one the restaurant will most likely give you a plastic bag) this doesnt add to the bulk at all. Than when we get home we wash it with dishsoap or even thrown in the top of the dishwasher! They are also very durable, I cant imagine them EVER becoming unusable... We found that bowls (yes, you will still need bowls!) with the suction cups on the bottom also stick well to this mat, maybe even better than the actual table! I also found them to be better than table toppers. Table toppers cost more (you have to continually buy new ones, you can only use them once) they dont have the "mote" to stop foods and drinks, they are too easy for baby to remove, and we found if the cups wet it can still make a ring around the table. Basically table toppers are just easier to travel with (fit in diaperbags easier)So the Goods->* Keep surfaces clean* Keep the floor cleaner* Protect tables from silverware and the rings from cups* Helps keep your baby/toddler cleaner* Has secure suction cups* Is easily washed/cleaned* Pretty cheap* VERY durable* Not TOO easy for children (at least our children) to remove* Better than table toppers (in our opinion)* Suction cup bowls fit wellThe not so Goods ->* Cant roll it up as well as it came* Takes up a bit of room in a diaperbag* You will need to replace the suction cups eventually (a CON? Maybe... but not a big deal)* Being inturupted durring EACH MEAL out to be asked where we got it :)... now is it a CON to be helping parents in need?Basically its all on your children, if they can remove it I am sure you wont be pleased with it... But I defiantly recommend purchasing one, its cheap and defiantly worth a shot!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I was thinking there must be a reusable placemat for babies and this is perfect. I ate at a restaurant yesterday with my 10 month old daughter. She fed herself her whole meal and only 2 cheerios and one piece of fruit ended up on the floor. The tray catches most of the food and then she can just eat what has fallen into the tray. It is so great not to leave a huge mess at a restaurant. Now when she starts throwing food on the floor on purpose, that will be another story.The suction cups need to get pretty wet in order to stick, but even when they aren\'t stuck down the mat doesnt\' move much.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: The mat is a good size and the tray really does catch the food my toddler misses. I would\'ve given it five stars but, though the material does keep it from sliding all over the place, the mat doesn\'t sunction to our wooden table very well.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: Easy to use, store and clean. Only downfall is it only sticks to smooth surfaces. My Daughter still hasn\'t been able to un-stick it herself yet, but she\'s only 15 months old.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: This is a very nice product. It collects the child\'s food, is easy to clean up and rolls up and tucks away very nicely. My only dislike is that it doesn\'t stick very well on our grooved table. You need a flat surface table for this to work properly.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I bought this for my baby when he was first starting finger foods.  It has been HEAVEN since!  I haven\'t had too much trouble with it not sticking to different surfaces- I\'ve only encountered one instance where it didn\'t stick, where the table was covered in a plasticy cloth cover.  Other than that, it stuck to wood, plastic, granite, you name it!My son (10months old) is still in the "pull everything up" and "everything in the mouth" stage, and I don\'t have any trouble with it at all.  It stays in place well.  The only part that flops up, is the tray thing that hangs over the table to pick up the things baby drops.  He likes to flip it up, and if I give him enough time to fiddle with it, he can start to rip it off the table.  But realistically, you\'ll hopefully be near your baby at all times while he\'s eating, so just curbing that behavior will take care of it.  No product will be perfect in that department, after all! :)The pocket is a life-saver though.  It\'s the main reason why I got this mat.  Also, someone reviewed it saying that it\'s hard to fold up...  I really disagree.  If you look at the back, it has little fold lines you follow, easily, and it rolls up up into the pocket, making it smaller than a rolled up handtowel.  Just fold the sides up and roll into the pocket.  Admittedly, if you fold to loosely to the sides, it wont fit in, but it\'ll take you to seconds to adjust that.Clean up is a snap too.  It\'s made of this rubbery latex (or something like it, I don\'t know), so you just run it under some hot water and wipe it down.  And this thing is made pretty well, so it\'s not like it\'ll fall apart by scrubbing it or messing around with it too much.All in all, I think it\'s a definete MUST HAVE for any one with a little one eating finger foods.  It\'s small, convenient, easy, durable, and most important you have a clean place for your little one to eat!Hope this was helpful!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I love this product because my son (11 mos old) loves to chew what\'s in front of him, tables included.  This product gives him something other than the germy restaurant table to chew, catches part of his food so he can still grab and eat it and gives us a place to cut and place his food.  Product does not keep baby from table (like one of the other reviews said), it is soft and squishable material.  Product is not hard to clean, you just have to rub and rinse under running water.  It rolls up and fits in any diaper bag - folds up on itself to contain the mess until you get home to clean.  What I don\'t like about the disposable table protectors is that my chewing son tears them to bits with his teeth, possibly ingesting plastic.  I suppose it depends on the mom and the baby but I recommend this product to every mom I know!!!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: This placemat is wonderful for small children!  My son eats by the handfuls, and the little scoop on the edge is great because it catches the food he drops.  I also like that it suctions to the table.  I\'m not giving this the full five stars, though, b/c sometimes the suction cups come off and the placemat rolls up on the sides.  But all in all, this is a wonderful item for small children!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I didn\'t have the problems that some write about (table clothes making the suction cups not work-- never went to those kids of resturants with my 1 year old! or trouble cleaning-- they clean well with a regular diaper wipe & then I would give it a good cleaning at home).  This item was a cost-effecitve alternative to those stick on one use placemats.  The little "trough" caught a lot of food.  My daughter is now two and long grew out of this as she easily eats off of a plate without trouble, so you won\'t need it forever.  I found it a great travel item; it rolls up well and fit into my diaper bag.  We even used it at home. I would highly recommend it.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: Had a lot of high hopes for this product...but then I just never used it. It sounds great but truthfully it was just too much trouble to carry it around (it\'s definitely not something small enough to fit in your purse, but maybe in a diaper bag if you want it taking up that much room). I would rather just wipe down the table, clean up after my son, and leave a bit higher tip if the kiddo takes to destroying his food while out.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I was unsure about spending so much money on a placemat for eating out.  But I must say, after using it a few times, it is FANTASTIC!  I can pull it out of the diaper bag and stick it right to the table.  There is a place to catch all the food that falls, and clean up is a cinch.  It rolls up and folds into itself for easy storage.  A MUST HAVE FOR ANY FAMILY THAT EATS OUT!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I saw someone out and about with this product in a restaurant one day and knew we had to have one!  I used to use the plastic mats with the adhesive on one side...this is MUCH easier to use and store!  I found the adhesive mats helpful but my daughter would pull them off the table because she liked the noise...with this...she does not!  I would recommend this for all parents!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: saw baby using it at mall, very neat.It helps parents a lot, and baby has fun eating too. I haven\'t used it yet, wait for my son to grow up, he may start to use it next month. I bought in advance.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: We use this all of the time.  My sons are just over two years old and we use this at the dinner table instead of the trays on their booster seats.  Many placemats are too busy with pictures, so they want to look at them.  My boys pick up placemats and the food goes everywhere.  This mat has plenty of suction cups to keep it in place and it is plain so the food is the interest and not pictures.  We also use this at restaurants.  My boys play with plates, and I don\'t like putting food directly on the table.  Who knows what the restaurant cleaned the table with?  Another plus is the scoop that hangs off of the table to catch spills.  The mat rolls up easily and compactly for storage even when it is messy.  I wipe as much food off as possible, then I roll it up and wash it at home.  I can fit two in my backpack along with all of our other supplies.  The only downfall is that tomato sauce stains it.  The stains eventually fade, just like a Tupperware container.  Another suggestion for these mats is to use with adults that have difficulty eating such as persons that have suffered a stroke or head injury.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I bought this thinking it would be great, but have been VERY disappointed.  The suction cups don\'t stick very well (especially on wood)even if you wet them first.  My daughter is able pull it right off the table and dump the mess on the floor.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: Perfect! Love it! Great for home and on the go. The suction cup works great and it cleans easily definitely cool!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I love this thing.  I\'ve had it for over a year.  We take it with us everywhere we go, so instead of worrying about cleaning off dirty restaurant tables we just put this down instead.  The long cup at the bottom helps to catch spills (not everything alas, but feeding a baby is never super-neat).  I also love how it rolls up nice and tight for easy transport.  And it\'s easy to clean.  Wouldn\'t recommend putting it in the dishwasher, however.  It did lose it\'s shape after a cycle.  Otherwise, I\'m very pleased with this purchase.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: We own two of them.  We use these CONSTANTLY as we go out.  They are the biggest lifesavers when we go out to eat.  They are easy to pack up as they fold up really nicely in themselves, they are very, very durable, they don\'t stain (easily), and they clean up really nice.  They are just spectacular.  We\'ve bought more for a few shower gifts for people, telling them that this is one of those things you won\'t realize that you need until you have kids and then use it.  Everyone we\'ve given it to loves them, too.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: We had a Kiddopotamuc Tinydiner when my 7 year old was a toddler and loved it. It lasted about two years when I finally threw it out because he didn\'t need it anymore.  When my two year old started sitting at the table a few months ago I rushed out to buy another one.  To my EXTREME disappointment, it was immediately obvious that they don\'t make them like they used it.When I took it out of the box, it had huge creases and to this day, will not lay flat.  I also made the mistake of putting it in the dishwasher.  The one I had 5 years ago was put in the dishwasher several times a week and came out looking fine.  The one I bought 4 months ago shriveled up the first time I put it in the dishwasher and will not take it\'s shape or stick to the table anymore.  It\'s also only 4 months in and the tray has completely ripped off.I used to recommend this placemat to all my new Mommy friends.  Unfortunately, I can no longer do that.  It is a crying shame that they had to go and cheap-out and ruin a perfectly wonderful product.  I eagerly await another company to step in and make a superior product.  My business will be all theirs.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: Hi to every busy Mom, easy cleanup! I have 4 kids under the age of 3 (a girl, 30 months, and triplets 15 month) I throw the place mats with the bibs in the washing machine on the gentle/handwash cycle and it is cleaned up. The "food catcher" avoids to big of a mess on the floor. The only drawback tomato sauce will stain the material.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: This placemat has been a great purchase!  I purchased it for use when we take our 9 month old out and it has been well received!  Not only does it cover the table, it catches some of the food items my son drops.  This is quite handy and an unexpected benefit.  Love it and so does my son.  He runs his hand over it, feeling all of the textures.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: I liked this mat, it\'s very functional and is so easy to carry on. The only thing is that in some tables the mat is not still but it\'s definitely the kind of table, otherwise I have no problems.

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: My husband and I saw a family out with this mat and we were fascinated. What a clever idea. Our son loves to pick up his food by himself. How many times to you see a waiter clean 5 tables with the same cloth. Also, do we really know how safe the cleaners they use are.We bought one for ourselves and for a friend, who was equally thrilled. Everytime we go out people ask where we got the mat from. They are so impressed how it stays in place and catches anything that may fall from small fingers, which can be quite a bit!One little note, the suctions cups don\'t work well on vinal tablecloths. Our son managed to detach the mat from the table and all his food ended up in his hair!

name: Kiddopotamus Tinydiner Placemat, Yellow
review: This placemat seemed like a terrific idea for eating out and eating at the table, but it has two fatal flaws:1) Even if the table is the kind of surface on which suction cups work (formica, glass), they\'re not so strong that a determined toddler (mine is 17 months) can\'t peel them right up.  The placemat becomes just one more toy to fling around.2) The catch trough is easily bent out of shape so that it catches nothing.We\'ll be sticking (pun intended) with the disposable adhesive mats, future landfill waste that they are.

name: Kidco Door Finger Guards
review: These finger guards work great and have lasted for many years now!  We use them for our children\'s bedrooms and hallway bathroom, to keep them from slamming doors shut and pinching fingers.  I especially like the feature of being able to "disable" it by simply turning it 90 degrees without taking the guard off the door frame, to let you close the door when needed.  The adhesive was not strong enough, so we just secured ours with screws, which I think was included (if not, just buy some at the hardware store).

name: Kidco Door Finger Guards
review: I have been using the door finger gaurds for a few weeks now. They do their job but the adhesive is very weak. I had to use super glue to get them to stick.

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: This thing makes me think that man never reached the moon.With all the intelligence in the world, why can\'t anyone come up with a good design for a formula dispenser?Please read my review on the Zo-Li dispenser as well to see what I mean.I bought this based on other people\'s reviews and thank god it\'s only $6, as it has a lot of flaws but it gets the job done - you just always have to be careful and wide awake when using it.Here are my gripes:1) The plastic it is made of is really hard and whenever I open the spout or the lid, I am this close to getting slivered.2) Formula definitely can transfer into other compartments when moved around in diaper bag as there is a gap between the lid and the dividing walls. Imagine workstation vs enclosed office.3) When you are half asleep as most moms are, and you accidentally have .001 of an inch of the spout open into the other compartment when pouring, the contents of the other compartment goes pouring in as well4) It is really hard to open the lid, which is not good because of problem no. 1 above. I am not kidding, my thumb is getting tiny blisters from opening the lid of the spout.5) The spout is round but the bins are pie shaped - and we learn this from kindergarten when we play with sorting cubes - triangles don\'t go in circles. Therefore, formula gets caught in the corners and it takes a lot of wiggling before everything goes out.The only thing I like about it is that I have been able to handle it with one hand and am still using it until I find something better - and it\'s not the Zo-Li.

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: The product works but it is not as pictured. I had specifically bought this brand because it is the same as one I had bought for my older son. The tab to open it is not as pictured and makes it difficult to use. I thought I made the mistake and didn\'t really it was their mistake until I already opened and used it. So beware!!

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: Ok product for little bottle (4oz). Formula did shift from one cell to another, which defeated the purpose of the pre-measuring option. I eventually gave up on the option and bought a thermos to hold hot water and pre-measured formula into each bottle - it was a lot easier in the end.

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: These are great to take along so that you don\'t have to carry a whole can of formula or try to pour premeasured formula out of a baggie or tupperware.  The chambers do mix a little at times but only when the lid isn\'t on tighly so make sure it snaps in place.  All in all it\'s a great item.

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: This is a great product if you on the road a lot. Just measure the amount of powder that you would need to make a bottle (for this product you can measure the powder for 4 bottles)and you don\'t have to bring the whole Enfamil container with you.

name: Sassy Baby Powdered Formula Dispenser, Colors May Vary
review: I ordered this item and was shipped something that seemed like a knockoff. The lid barely stayed on and ended up opening all over my purse. If I could return it just for the principle of doing so I would. They should also reimburse me for my new diaper bag. The only thing worse would have been spilled breast milk.

name: Toilet Lock
review: Don\'t let the crappy photo fool you. This is by far the best toilet lock for ease of adult use and safety. The rest of the products (my wife bought several) are cheap and may not even fit most toilets (again, a problem with several of them). Buy this product with confidence. Just bought my second for the other bathroom now that the kid can open door knobs.

name: Toilet Lock
review: I have tried several different types of toilet lid locks and they all have some kind of adhesive that does not stick and so they end up in the trash a day or so later (sometimes just hours later) and are a complete waste of money.  This lock has no adhesive and is very sturdy.  The arm is stiff enough to prevent the lid from opening very far and it installs with only a screw driver on the back of the toilet seat.  You just unscrew the lid and place it over the holes then screw the lid back on.  It has an adjustment screw on the side to change the height for thicker lids or covers and the best part of it is that the arm swings back by itself when you close the lid.  You don\'t have to remember to re-lock the seat every time you use it!  Great idea for a house with older kids who will not remember to lock up!  It can be moved out of the way if you need to by pulling up on the arm and swinging it out to the side.  Very easy operation, just push the button in with one hand and push the arm back toward the tank and lift the seat.  It does require two hands to operate.  The only problem I had with it was when we had an 8 year old boy stay over with our son and he forgot it was there in the middle of the night.  He pulled the seat up with some force and the button and part of the side broke off of the pivot part of the lock. It still works but we have to lift the arm to move it instead of using the button.  It still keeps the little ones (18 months and 2 and half years) from getting into it.  I would definitely buy these again if I had too.  They seem like they will last long enough for the kids to out grow their curiosity with the toilet through.

name: Toilet Lock
review: The idea is brilliant, but the execution is flawed.The base bracket is thick, which causes the toilet seat to be not level with the toilet.  Many people have broken seats because of this.Despite being thick, the base is not rigid enough.  With the swing arm in place (on a now not-level seat which creates an automatic 1 cm gap), a child can still lift the seat.  (The seat acts like a lever upon the swing arm which end up torquing the base plate.)  Then they can stick their hand or arm in.There is a single set screw that sets against the plastic arm in a way that is not secure.  With enough force, the arm can be removed from the base completely.  Although this may seem like a stretch, you have to remember that the toilet seat acts like a lever when pressing against the swing arm, and the child\'s lifting force is amplified.Worse, the arm can lift off the base even without slipping from the set screw because it is held down only by the internal spring.  When this happens, the lid can snap back into place when you release it.With this design, worst case, a child could raise the lid just far enough to get his head inside and then the lid could snap down on his back clamping him inside.My nine month old baby is able to lift the lid enough to get his hands inside the toilet.I worry this "safety device" is more of an un-safety device and strongly recommend you look elsewhere.

name: Toilet Lock
review: After installing this toilet lock as directed, I found that the lid could still be opened wide enough for a young child to put in their head and upper-body. Thus, this \'safety device\' could then possibly trap the child by making it difficult to pull themselves back out. I\'ve tried several other toilet locks and have finally realized that they are a waste of time and I will simply rely on tight supervision rather than gimmicks/gadgets that could possibly do more harm than good.

name: Toilet Lock
review: This lock keeps my three little ones from exploring the toilet when I\'m otherwise occupied.  The best lock is a closed bathroom door, but when you have to keep it open, this keeps the kids from playing in the water or tossing things in.  They can\'t see inside so the entertainment value isn\'t there.  A very determined older child can break it with brute strength however.

name: Toilet Lock
review: This is great at keeping tots from jumping IN to the toilet and getting in to trouble or worse.However, if your lid is thin and "stylish" rather than thick and stury as the one that is pictured, it may be flexible enough to bend.  In our case, even with everything tightened as much as possible, it still leaves a gap big enough for little hands to sneak things into the toilet...Overall, we are pleased with the purchase, and recommend it.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I love this little food mill.  I had one for both my children, and have now gotten one for my granddaughter.  It\'s so simple, and so convenient.With all the fancy, expensive things out there, this still does everything you need it to at a ridiculously reasonable price.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Great product. Easy to use EXCEPT putting the grinding lid on. It\'s a little bit frustrating to get it in just the right place so it will snap in. Easy to clean, but wish they\'d fix that darn top part.Highly recommended! It will grind just about anything (we\'ve tried things like fruit salad to steak to shepherd\'s pie! Comes out perfect every time!)

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I bought it from Mary go round. First time I liked it so much. I started to give my 5 month old son apples and bananas... but than I\'ve tried to make broccoli pure..It was pretty hard to grind it..So this product just for soft food.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Stick with your food processor.  Hard to turn, hard to clean, accommodates very little food.  Not worth the price, however low it may be.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I wish I\'d known before I bought this product that the grinding strainer is now made of plastic. WhenI first bought one of these devices in the early 80s the strainer was made of metal. It would grind up anything. Now it\'s made of plastic. On the first attempt to grind up 3 oz. of tender roast beef, it failed miserably. It just would not do it, regardless of the amount of pressure applied. The device also leaks out of the bottom.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Unlike many of the negative reviews, I am very happy with this item. We use it about 2-4 times a day and it\'s very effective and easy to use.It requires some strength to push down, but it is really minimal and takes less than 2 minutes to use for one type of food (I\'m 120lbs and have very little upper body strength) and I have no trouble.[...]It\'s SO easy that was the first thing I was going to say... I give it a good hot rinse after I\'m done with it, so the food doesn\'t dry up, but not much else. At night I wash (with a bristle brush) around the rubber ring and the strainer part with soap and hot water. i could put it in the dishwasher, but haven\'t yet because I don\'t think it needs it.The reason I give it 4 stars is only because the handle isn\'t super sturdy. It\'s made of plastic, which hasn\'t caused a problem yet (it\'s 3 months old) but I can\'t imagine I\'ll be using it for my grandchildren 20 years in the future.[...]

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: This mill is one of the best things I\'ve ever purchased for my baby.  No more baby food for the most part.  Now, he can just eat what we are having, within reason.  It saves time and money for me.  Works great, especially if you crank the handle fast.  I\'m surprised what will go through it!

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: My sister-in-law used one of these with her children and loved it.  So, naturally when we started having kids she gave one to us.  It is GREAT!  I was able to feed my children whatever we were eating.  Not having to buy baby food saved a lot of money.  I didn\'t have to worry about carrying heavy jars of food around and worrying that they might break in my diaper bag.  This grinder is so durable. I used it with both of my children who are 3 years apart in age as well as now having gone through 4 neices and nephews.  My oldest is now 10.  It will even grind meat.  Most other baby food grinders only do cooked fruits or vegies.  I am currently looking for another one for a nephew.  My old one is still being used by another nephew.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: This grinder is so easy to use and I like being able to give my baby foods that I have made myself.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: The food mill is ok, but not as great as I expected. It\'s hard to push down while grinding and keeping the mill in place. The system to keep the actual handle, blade, and grate on the mill doesn\'t work very good. I\'m not sure if I\'m doing something wrong, so it could be user error, it just seems like it should be easier than it is, so I don\'t use it very often. Also, some of the reviews mentioned grinding meat, but I haven\'t found it to be able to do that. It sometimes has trouble with the less soft fruits and veggies, and always leaves bits and pieces that it can\'t reach. Overall, not something I\'d recommend.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I bought one of these 3 yrs ago when my first son was small. This one had a stainless steel blade and strainer. It worked great! Easy to use, disassemble, wash. Then, I lost it and had to get another. The current plastic strainer is VERY difficult to take off of the base, it doesn\'t grind food well unless it\'s very soft and it\'s hard to clean. Overall, the product has gone way downhill as far as quality and ease of use. If the stainless blade were to return, I\'d give it 5 stars.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: My son is only 10 months and refuses to eat baby food. I now just take my KidCo Food Mill, put whatever the rest of my family is having for meals into it, grind it up and feed it to the baby. He loves eating "real" food but doesn\'t have many teeth. Because of this the Mill works great for us.The Mill is easy to use and easy to clean. Great product!

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: This food mill is useful for "soft" food items. Useful for bananas, cooked apple etc. Doesnt work very well if the fruit/vegetable isnt soft.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: The food mill allows you to feed your baby what ever you like, by making it easy to serve anywhere and anytime.  No stinking batterries or electric cords.  They see what you have, now they can have it!  Agape\' Jan Droegemeyer

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I had something like this when my boys were babies 30 years ago. It meant we didn\'t have to buy expensive \'baby food\' which we couldn\'t afford anyway. I was delighted to find one for my daughter-in-law. Yes, they can be a pain to clean sometimes but that is far outweighed by the benefits of having food you can trust for your baby.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: The food mill is very easy to use and clean up afterwards. I have used it to mash up boiled veggies (cauliflower/squash, peas come out esp. well) and banana. The food mashes well, not thoroughly pureed like jarred food, but well enough for my 8 mo. old who as yet has no teeth but is learning to use her jaws. For the price, esp. it is a very good buy.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Quality of material was as expected for the price but unfortunately the grinder mechanism does not come flush with the platform hence the food does not get grinded.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: this product does what it says and is handy but you have to really push hard on it so the food gets pushed up and so the wheel can grind it. VERY MESSY! I used the storage containers you can buy sepratly more than i used the actual grinder.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I have used baby food mills before when all 4 of my children were babies, a different brand.  This product was a big disappointment and did not work well at all.  The top grinding piece is plastic (not metal) and was very difficult to process the food through. On anything other than soft vegetables, I had to often ask someone to help by pressing down on the cylinder while I turned the handle. It has no gasket at the bottom of the cylinder and any liquid would run all over the counter. I would not recommend this mill to anyone, it was a waste of money, I quit using it after a week.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: This was part of a gift pack and I took a chance as I did not know if this was going to be a jarred baby food family.  I was pleased to find out they were already planning to make their own baby food and were glad to get the grinder.  I got the portable hand cranked one because that was what i used.  Wonderful at all time but especially on trips.  Just take food off your own plate, grind it and feed it to baby!!!!  Healthier and a great cost saver.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: 30 years ago I used one of these products and it was the way I "nurished  children"  between breast feeding and "real people food".I give this gift to all new moms.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: It\'s so cute and helpful for babies, with easy clean and safe.Be aware only for sharpness tool. Thanks ,

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I have used this mill for about 6 months on a regular basis for pureeing all kinds of vegetables and fruits; sweet potatoes, peas, apples, pears, bananas, cooked rice and lentils, cherries, oranges, etc; some steamed (sweet potatoes) others raw (oranges, cherries)and this has worked beautifully every single time.Only reason for four stars is after repeated and extensive use this mill has gotten scratched and nowadays I worry about it not getting washed throroughly especially because of the nicks and scratches-maybe use of more durable and BPA free plastics (not sure if this is currently BPA free) would be advisable.Overall a good product, definitely a more economical alternative to buying jarred food, although I have resorted to that on occasion for convenience.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Kidco needs to redesign this to solve two problems:1) the plate/handle/blade component is difficult to take on and off, especially if there is food in the tubing (I own the oval one - perhaps the round one is different. The shape makes it harder to get your hands down in there and twist).2) unacceptably, about a half inch of food is left in the bottom after you\'ve ground down as far as it will go.I jumped on here to write this review after I tried to mash up spaghetti noodles with chicken sauce for my daughter. The noodles and saucy part did just fine, but the chunks of chicken remained in the bottom, untouched. So I removed them and cut them up by hand. Now....what did I need the grinder for again?

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Picked this grinder up at the food co-op. It seemed a bit simple but I was willing to give it a try. We had tried making baby food using the blender, but had trouble getting the consistency right, plus I hate trying to clean out the bits of food stuck around the blade.We\'ve also tried mashing and mincing, but we couldn\'t get the texture right. Our granddaughter was still gagging on the bits of minced meat or vegetable.The first night had the grinder, we put a little of what we were eating (including the meat) into the chamber and began turning the blade as we pushed down on the cylinder. The ground food coming up through the little holes was not as silky smooth and airy as a blended version, but smoother than a chopped version. Not only did  she eat it all up quickly, but now when we start eating, she makes it clear that we need to grind some up for her.So instead of making a special batch of baby food, we just bring the grinder to the table with us.It\'s small enough to drop into the diaper bag to take to restaurants and I personally think it\'s easier to wash than the blender.Simple inexpensive alternative to jars of partially-eaten baby food.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: The first food I wanted to use was broccoli.  It would work wonderfully, then seemed to get jammed, work again, etc.  It does work, but with more effort than I had expected.  I tried preparing the food to be softer, but I encountered the same problems.  I tried nectarines another day, and it made it very soupy.  I guess I wish there was a way to adjust the mechanism to grind the food to different consistencies.  My 9 month old son can handle chunkier foods, but with this mill the food is very liquidy.  The size and minimal amount of parts/assembly make it very convenient and very easy to move.  Also the entire mill can be cleaned in the dishwasher.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I bought this food mill, based on the reviews & the price, in order to make homemade baby food.  Sadly, as much I wanted to love it, this food mill is piece of junk.The base is sturdy enough, but other parts are very flimsy.  For example, you have an assembly containing a blade, a sieve & a handle.  This assembly is very poorly made.  It\'s hard to fit onto the base b/c it\'s so flimsy & you may find it impossible if your hands get wet during the process.Then, after you are lucky enough to get the entire food mill assembled, the actual process of chopping up the food is a nightmare.  You must push down on the base (in order to position the food pieces to be chopped) while turning this flimsy handle.  Mine always got stuck.  I *can* multi-task so pushing down & turning a handle shouldn\'t have presented me with such drama, but I could never get more than a teaspoon of food to blend before getting annoyed and dumping out my hard-earned work.I can\'t say that I have a better solution right now.  I\'m going back to Amazon to hopefully find a better piece of equipment.  But, for your own sanity, stay away from this item.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: This food mill is of the same design as the one we used more than 30 years ago when our children were small. [All learned to enjoy fresh and wholesome foods and continue to have healthy eating habits.]I just bought 2 food mills; one for our house and another for our daughter and son-in-law so any one of us could make \'instant baby food\' from foods that are part of a family meal.  A healthy and economical way to introduce a baby to new foods.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I LOVE this product!  I was reluctant to buy one for my first child, but I got one the second time around!!!!  I don\'t know how I survived without it!!!!!!  I just put some of MY food in there...at home or at a restaurant....add a LITTLE water to make it the perfect consistancy...and whallah!!!!  PERFECT baby food!!!!!!!!!!  LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE this product!

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I broke two of these trying to strain peas & green beans. You really have to over cook/steam the vegetables for this to work well. My friend who has to puree her daughter\'s food for the rest of her life recommended the bullet. I\'ve been using it & it\'s the best so far. More expensive but i also use it for myself(chopping onion & smoothies). It\'s also about the same size of this food mill that\'s hard to use. My son is 18 months now & I still make his apple sauce with the bullet that I\'ve had for about a year now.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I don\'t really understand the negative reviews.  If you order it, realize what you\'re getting.  You\'re not getting a powerful food grinder that will grind meats, raw vegetables or undercooked foods.  Of course the food must be well cooked.  You can\'t feed a baby "crisp tender" vegetables.For $13 it pays for itself in a week.  Cook some green beans till very tender, pop them in, turn the crank and out comes baby food.  Same with carrots, squash, sweet potatoes, etc. Actually it\'s so easy a four year old can do it.We do bananas and grapes nearly every day.  If we want apple we\'ll cook it till it\'s tender.It\'s great for on the go as well.  The baby is too young right now but I\'m sure it would grind up cooked shrimp and fish in a snap...

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: The Food Mill arrived quickly, but I am going to return this item because it is missing the grinder plate.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: Warped, hard to push together to use or pull apart to clean. Being returned. The Munchkin is a superior product.

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: We like mealtime to be a family affair from the beginning so we love to sit the baby down and grind up whatever we are eating so they can participate. Great, easy, and wholesome homemade food for you baby!

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: It works great and was shipped in a timely manner.  Our baby can now eat all the food we eat and she loves it!

name: Food Mill - BabySteps Kid Co 1 Pk
review: I had an older model of this food mill (the reason I purchased this one) and the plastic and metal grinding materials were much more substantial.  I would have preferred paying a little more and getting the quality of the original version.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: My son has had poor latch issues that have made BFing difficult and painful.  I had hoped that this shield would help but it is so big and bulky that he can\'t latch on at all with this thing. My baby isn\'t a small baby either.  He was 12 lbs at birth (11 now) and is very healthy.  So for us this was a waste of money and I can\'t recommend it all.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I so wish i was able to breastfeed without this little piece of plastic, but apparently its not going to happen. because of bleeding/cracked nipples, ineffective latching by my children my first child was exclusively pump/bottle fed. that lasted 6 months. my second child i discovered the shield and i lasted 9 months. my third baby i went to the shield on day 3, and were at 5 weeks now. there is no way i would be able to feed them without. and after pumping exclusively for 6 months, this little thing has been a lifesaver! yes, it is a pain to make sure i have it with us, but worth it!

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: Was hoping to use this to entice baby to latch on, but it didn\'t work as expected. It was just awkward and didn\'t work in the way I had expected it to. This was my experience.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: We took a breastfeeding class and the teacher never mentioned this.  I had the hardest time when my son was born with latching on.  It hurt so much and it would take 45 mins to get him latched on.  I would recommend this to everyone.  I wish I would have known about it before.  Would have saved me 3 days of tears.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: my baby would not latch starting day 3 so I started using the nipple shield as a temporary solution, because the baby latched right on to it and the "contact" is definitely the best one out there. however, he would not ween off of it and latch to my nipple after weeks of trying. breastfeeding also became extremely painful with the shield on or off. my boy is now 8 weeks, i have seen multiple lactation consultants, my midwives & doctors, i have gotten his tongue tie clipped, been treated for everything under the sun and still no latch! i think that the nipple shield delayed proper treatment and allowed him to develop a preference for artificial nipples. although i\'m still trying to breastfeed daily i usually use a bottle... still hopeful!

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I have a particularly small child.  She was 6 lbs at birth but completely healthy.  I purchased this item in hopes to get some relief for my sore nipples.  The product is bigger than a bottle nipple.  It\'s to wide and sticks out to far.  It gagged her so she would not use it.  I\'m sure it probably works for some people but I had a Medela Nipple shield with my first child that covered all of the areola and was a better fit.  This one is bulky.  I may have ordered the wrong size so I would say contact a lactation consultant or your hospital\'s doula for help.  The one I used that worked (4 years ago) was given to me in the hospital.  I had to order this one online since we are military and stationed overseas.  I did like that the baby gets more skin to skin contact with this item...so if your child isn\'t a petite little one...they may like it.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: Great tool to use just be careful of lowered milk production and clogged ducts.  The nurses in the hospital gave this to me because my baby was not comfortable with the latch.  Turned out she had an attached frenulum (upper lip) and may have not latched in the beginning because of it.  This got us started and about a month in I transitioned without it because if you don\'t have one around it\'s panic time!  Also, I was getting clogged ducts because it\'s harder for babies to pull all of the milk out with the shield.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: The hospital lactation consultants really pushed this item. Know that this is detrimental to your milk supply. The baby cannot successfully compress the sinuses around the nipple if he latches on to this shield as he will suck more like he would a bottle. It took me 5 very long and frustrating weeks to wean my baby from this thing. That was time I could have spent enjoying my baby rather than fighting with him. Giving him whole, natural breast milk is extremely important to me or I would have given up and just went to formula. A friend of mine gave up on breast feeding all together when faced with the same problem. The same consultants at the same hospital pushed it on her as well.If you have flat or inverted nipple know that you do not need an aid. Your baby knows no other nipple and will figure it out. Once the La Leche League leader in my area told me this, it gave me the strength to go for weaning my baby from it.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: it work but slips off all the time.too much let dowwn of milk and it is hard to remove the baby off of it

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: Life saving! My nipples were so sore & cracked I wanted to give up. Had a friend tell me about the nipple shields  & now I nurse with zero pain!

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: My lactation consultant suggested that I try the nipple shield.  My baby was having a hard time trying to latch on but she was fine with sucking from a bottle.  I used the nipple shield for about a week and when I stopped, the baby would latch on no problem.  As an added benefit, baby can easily switch between breast or bottle.  I would use this definitely again with the next baby.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I had a cracked nipple before I even left the hospital.  After almost two weeks of ointments, tears and toes gripped into the floor each time I had to nurse - a lactation consultant recommended I try this for a little bit.  It\'s important to measure your nipple and get the right size!  Using this for a few days allowed my nipple to heal and helped nursing become bearable.  Once the nipple healed I was able to try nursing w/o the shield again and everything fell into place.  My baby had no trouble going back to a bare breast.  I am so thankful these were out there.  I had never heard of them and they saved my breastfeeding experience.  My baby is six weeks old now and everything is going great!!  Don\'t give up, these can really help!! :)

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: While I could think of plenty of negative things to say about the nipple shield if I really wanted to, I am giving this product 4 stars. It was the only way I was able to nursed my LO when he was first born. We tried a dozen or more times to get him to latch on to my inverted nipple, as well as my flat one. Every time, he fussed and cried. As a first time mother, I was already stressed at the idea of nursing. The nurses offered me the nipple shield to try and some sugary water to put on it so that the baby would take to it more easily. I had several nurses with several opinions, and I would encourage anyone considering using the nipple shield to listen to any advice they can get about it. I was given the advice that I should use it as long as the baby needed from one nurse. My midwife said that I would know when he didn\'t need it anymore when I stopped reaching for it to nurse him. Another nurse said that she always worried that the baby would not get enough hindmilk when using the nipple shield. Another just tried shoving it down his throat in the middle of the night. Family members reacted in a variety of ways to seeing it, too.Ultimately, what many reviews say is true. The baby becomes dependent upon the nipple shield very quickly and easily. I was extremely frustrated that he wouldn\'t nurse without it and disheartened that he would cry hysterically whenever I tried to latch him without it, but I tried at least a couple of times a week. Over time, he started to go on nursing strikes in the afternoons when he was overtired and hungry, and I attribute that to the fact that the baby was not getting milk in his belly as quickly as he wanted. He had to in essence fill up the nipple shield to fill up his mouth. It is not nearly as efficient as nursing from a real nipple (as I found out when numerous people remarked about how long it was taking him to nurse). One day, when he was 11 weeks old, he decided he was tired of the middle man (the nipple shield) and nursed (ON BOTH SIDES!!!) without it. I could not believe it. And he did it again the next time I went to feed him. And the next time.I truly thought I was going to be stuck using it for as long as I (or he) chose to nurse. My advice to anyone who chooses to nurse using the nipple shield, and who really wishes they could nurse without it, is to try every once in a while to see if the baby will latch without it. Be patient! Just like everything else, the baby will do it in his/her own time.Pros:Can save a nursing relationship that would otherwise have never startedHelped with bottle feedingDoes pull out the inverted/flat nipple enough to help with latching (over time for me)A great conversation starterEven if they are less efficient than nursing without them, baby will still grow and thriveCheaper than formula!Cons:Clear! Whoever thought of making these clear was crazy. They are so easy to lose in the couch cushions, on the floor, on the counter, and they can easily get swept up and thrown into the trash. Be careful. They are too expensive to be throwing away.Messy! If you don\'t get a good seal on these puppies, they leak like crazy. I can\'t tell you how many time I had milk all over myself after he ate.Makes nursing in public (or around family/friends who stare and ask lots of questions) a little more challenging for self conscious individuals.Babies do become dependent on them. Have one on hand at all times.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: Nice fit but apparently baby did not care for...it was natural feeling. And even after washing it smelled like plastic

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: My 6 day old son was having a issue with his latch because he could not keep his tongue down.  He would get frustrated and would not feed so we had to use a bottle, and pump.  After we got this we went home and followed the instructions.  All that consisted of was to clean the shield and run it in warm water for a few seconds and put it on the nipple after that start to breast feed.  it is that easy it solved the issue and took 2 seconds to latch on and feed for the first time like he should for a hour and a half. After this we know it worked because he went into what we call a milk coma.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I had the hardest time getting my son to latch on. The nurses were working with me at every feeding but he just refused to stay latched! I was so close to quitting. But a nurse had given me one of these and it was amazing! I didn\'t have a hard time getting him to latch on and stay on! He got so use to it that he wouldn\'t nurse without it.I now use it with my daughter. She was a very sleepy baby and had a hard time latching on in the hospital, so I made sure I brought one of these shields with me. After a few weeks I tried nursing her without it and she latched on without the shield just fine! (See girls really are smarter than boys, so naa-naa-boo-boo!)I continue to nurse my daughter using the shield because it\'s just so much easier to get her to latch on under a nursing cover, easier in case I\'m engorged, and if she decides she\'s done and comes off while I\'m in the middle of a let down we don\'t have a messy mess because it pools up in the shield for a few seconds giving me time to grab a spit up rag.Now that I\'m around more moms with kids around the same age as mine, I\'ve heard a few of them tell me that if they had known about these nursing shields that they probably would have breastfed their child instead of switching to formula.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: This was like a miracle in helping my premature baby latch on and nurse for more than a minute or two. It stays in place and fit well, they come in a variety of sizes.  It seemed very large at first but once my baby got going and the nipple got sucked into the shield it was obviously the right size.  I am so please with these because they make breast feeding possible for us.  I was pumping but that can be very hard on your nipples and make them very sore, breast feeding is much more gentle in the long run.  One thing I don\'t like is the cut out, I would prefer the "regular" version. This is a personal preference and does not affect the functionality so I still give the product 5 stars!

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: Struggled a lot with breastfeeding at first, and this helped the transition to feeding without it. It is a little annoying to find and clean, but the purpose that it served saved me and enabled me to bridge the gap between learning to latch and feeding normally.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: This was a life saver! Only thing is that I wish I had gotten the regular nipple shield instead of the contact because the cutout prevents it from adhering perfectly. But still, it adheres pretty well and saved me from exhaustion of pumping every time she was hungry (which I did for two and a half weeks before I discovered this) and helped me to transition from a bottle to proper nursing. She is now able to do without the shield but it literally saved us!

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I used these for my first daughter since she had a tough time latching on. They are safe for baby\'s mouth and it aids very well in feeding. Those who are striving to breastfeeding for a while may love this if your baby isn\'t latching on well. After our son came along I haven\'t had to use these once since he latches on well (he\'s only 2 weeks old) but they are good to have when it\'s 3am and you want baby to feed and you want to sleep. It\'s comfortable and made well. Easy to clean with just mild soap and hot water.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I don\'t think that I could have breastfed without this and it is the only reason that I continued breastfeeding.  I never had cracked or bleeding nipples.  I did not have flat or inverted nipples. I ended up buying three (just to have extras on hand because you feed more often than you can wash them).  My baby was born early and stayed in the NICU. The nurses there are adamant about your trying to breastfeed.  I heard so many horror stories.  The nurses gave me this my first day and I never had any trouble.  For the first two weeks, we used this every time he ate.  Then we used it off and on for about three more weeks (5 weeks total).  Then, by that time, we both learned how to do it and he could nurse from my breast without any aid (how to latch, how to cup your breast, etc).  My baby is now 3.5 months old and we exclusively breast feed.  He has never had nipple confusion (though we do give him a pacifier and he eats pumped milk from a bottle - but he nurses every day from the breast as well).  I feel like a dairy & I have never had trouble with supply.  At the three month checkup, my son was in the 87th percentile for weight (and that is compared to normal babies, not preemies).  It is so inexpensive to at least get one to have on hand and give it a shot.

name: Medela Contact Nipple Shield - Standard Size (24mm)
review: I was introduced to this by a lactation consultant with my second baby about a week into breastfeeding. When my milk comes in, it COMES IN! With both my sons I became so engorged that it was difficult for them to latch on. I would have to pump for a few minutes & then have them latch on. The nipple shield helps baby latch on & not get overwhelmed with all the milk coming at them for the first few minutes. Then I take it off when the breast is less taut & put baby back on for the duration of the feeding. It was so helpful with my second baby to help get us through the first month or so. It also helped soothe tough, cracked & bleeding nipples with the initial latch when that was an issue. Once things got regulated I stopped using the sheild. I nursed him for 13 months! Now I\'m getting ready for #3 & will have one before baby even arrives.

name: KidCo On/Off Appliance Lock
review: I have a 3 and 4 year old and this device did little to deter or prevent them from raiding the fridge while their mom and I were asleep. A couple of good, hard yanks by your child and this device fails. This might me a good product for infants and toddlers, but if your child is over 2 years old, try something else like the Lock Release Fridge Latch by Safety 1st (but be aware that even though these are by far superior, you\'ll still have to place about 3 of these Safety 1st latches on your fridge door to keep the little ones from defeating them. That\'s what worked for us anyway. I\'ll be so glad when they grow out of this fridge fascination.)

name: KidCo On/Off Appliance Lock
review: It took my 2 1/2 year old son appproximately 5 minutes to rip this thing off my refridgerator. The idea is simple and seems like it should work. However, the type of glue that is used does not stand up to a child with any determination.

name: KidCo On/Off Appliance Lock
review: This thing seems to be working fairly well (through 2 weeks). However, I was surprised how rudimentary the thing works. It takes very careful mounting in order to function. I am surprised that I didn\'t have to redo mine after I mounted it the first time.

name: Wrap-n-ride Warm and Cozy Carrier Liner
review: Though I have seen many of the plaid baby seat cover ups in use, when I went to search for it this one caught my eye instead because one reviewer commented how this did not limit the face hole to a specific location. Very true! It made taking my baby everywhere so much easier. I was able to dress my baby in regular clothes & put him in the car seat easily. The hood protected him well against snow & wind. It was one of the best things we bought, and was reasonably priced!

name: Wrap-n-ride Warm and Cozy Carrier Liner
review: This product is absoultely wonderful.  It fits perfectfully on my son\'s Evenflo carseat and always keeps him comfortable and warm.  I couldn\'t imagine having to take him in and out of a snowsuit every time we go somewhere.  It is so easy to just put him in and zip him up, and pull the hood over his head.  When I get him in the car I just upzip it halfway, fold the hood back, and go.  I was also very greatful for this one night when I accidently locked my six week old son and myself out of the house in the twenty degree weather.  We were outside for almost twenty minutes before we were able to get inside and I was very worried that my son would get cold.  When I got him inside, I unzipped the wrap and ride.  He was still asleep and felt as warm as ever.  The price is a bargain compared to similar products and is truly a value.  I just hope that my son( who is big for his age)does not outgrow his carseat before the end of winter so we can continue to use this product!!

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: These blankets are WONDERFUL!  ESPECIALLY if you want to swaddle your baby.  The blankets are rectangle instead of square, this helps to keep the ends tucked in.  I still use them to tuck in my toddler, the large size continues to come in very handy.

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: I bought these receiving blankets when my son was first born back in November. I used them to swaddle him for almost a month.  These blankets are very good size.  After the first month, I cannot swaddle him anymore because he\'s an "escape artist" who always manage to get one of his arm or leg out side of the blankets. The blankets held up well after washes.  Now the weather are getting warmer.  I\'m using them as light blankets for warm nights.  They are excellent.  Definitely worth the money.

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: We received this as a gift and have loved them.  The blankets are large and quite soft.  Some of the other receiving blankets that we received were too small (even for our 7 pound baby).  We went back and purchased a few more after our son was born.

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: These receiving blankets are extra large and perfect to completly cover you while breast feeding.  Additionaly they are great for a bigger baby that you need to wrap up (Swaddle).  They wash up nice also.  God Bless You!

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: These blankets were on my registry... i put them there after i read the reviews here. But on the very first wash, they began to give way around the edges and started to fray... very unsightly.I give 5 stars for the fabric...very soft...but the fraying spoils it.

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: These are great blankets to use for swaddling and just for covering up the baby.  They are soft and hold up well after washing.  The 220 thread count is excellent.  This is a must Buy!

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: We received a number of receiving blankets for our son\'s baby shower, including Carters, Wamsutta, and these.  After 8 months these are still my favorites.  The Wamsutta blankets (30" square) were just too small, and the Carters blankets were cut odd - after a number of washings I noticed the corners no longer match up when I fold them, and they are nowhere near as soft as these Koala Baby blankets.  I still use these for my 8 month old as a summer blanket (not swaddled) for naptimes and nighttimes.  These are the softest receiving blankets we own, and the first ones I pull out of the drawer if we need a light cover for our little boy.

name: Koala Baby 4 Pack Receiving Blankets - Boy Assortment
review: please do not buy this particular itemit\'s VERY low quality

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: We actually got this so that our cat would stop opening our closet doors, and it does the trick.  However, I think our doors have a bigger gap than what is ideal, because it doesn\'t take much force to open them without pushing in the tabs on the lock.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: I saw these at a friend\'s house and when my baby started opening his closet, I knew I needed to get these.  They work great!  My little one figured out quick that he can\'t open the door anymore and gave up.  I looked around for the best deal and found them here on Amazon.com.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: This product is completely worthless.  We have doors exactly like the ones shown in the picture, with the fake laminate wood, and the adhesive does not stick at all.  As soon as you push down on the butterfly wings to open your door, it bows in the center of the lock, which lifts the adhesive portion off the door, and then it just pops right off.  And once it pops off, it\'ll never stick again.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: this product IS cheap, but it works for now. really, we have no other options that i can find, so i am stuck with this- until it breaks. one thing i really suggest doing is measuring the distance between doors. i didn\'t think there was much of a gap between the doors, but there is. i had to very carefully bend the flaps up a little more so it would catch on the door. once my kids see that if i pull out on the door a little to open it, this will be useless. i am just counting the days until that happens or it breaks. though, i would buy this again because I HAVE NO OTHER OPTIONS! lol!

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: This gadget worked great for a couple of days.  But someone pushed a little too hard and it popped off.  I had cleaned the area before applying the adhesive, so I thought it would last longer than it did.  I put on a second one and it did the same thing.  It also took off some of the paint from my sliding door.  It is a wonderful concept, and I\'m actually thinking of putting a different adhesive on the back of it and trying again, because I loved it while it was working.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: These are perfect for our mirror closet sliders, but they break so easily--be sure to buy them by the dozen!

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: Of the options available, this is a decent one, however, you need to make sure that you install these above any panel designs in the door so that it does not get caught in the grooves of the panel and get stuck. You also need to accept the fact that the back of the adjacent door will get some wear and tear from the lock rubbing against the surface.

name: Sliding Door Locks
Sliding Door Locks
review: Easy for me to use, but keeps my daughter out.  I ended up having to use command strips because the adhesive that came with the locks wouldn\'t stay on my door even I put it on before bed so that it had 10 hours to set before using it.  Not a big deal to me, other than it took the paint off the door which was factory painted so I can\'t fix it without repainting the whole thing.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: My doors have a frame around them so the "wings" don\'t stand out far enough to do any good ...at all.  As they are glass doors, I wasn\'t concerned about adhesives.  If you have wood, I think the adhesive would ruin the finish.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: These were great in theory, but did not work for me. Of the two that came in the pack, one would not stick to the door, and the other stuck but popped off after about 4 uses. The one that popped off took a fair amount of paint and wood off the door as well. My child was unable to open the door while it was installed, but the locks would not stay on with normal use. Seller was quick to ship, and price was great. I will keep looking for a better solution for the kids closet.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: These have worked well to keep our twin toddlers from opening the sliding closet doors.  Our childcare provider, on the other hand, has broken two of them because she forces the doors without thinking about pushing the wings in.  Fortunately, they still work with only one wing!  For those who have bad reviews, I wonder if the wings were on backward.  Notice the direction of the straight vs angled sides.  Also, I\'d suggest using a better adhesive for longevity.  We\'d buy again; in fact, we have already.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: I couldn\'t wait to install these to keep our toddler from getting in to mischief.  However, two good pulls on the door and the plastic piece came flying off and the baby now had free access and a choking hazard. It definately was not strong enough to handle a child that knew how to open the door.  Not what I had hoped for.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: im still trying to figure out how to use this product...im keeping it because im sure someday someone will know what to do

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: We have twin 3-year-old boys, and these wings have been the best safety device we\'ve used yet.  They are very strong boys (and often work together at trying to pry things open), and they have yet to overpower this lock (we\'ve been using them for over a year).  The important details about installing this lock is to make sure you put it up high on the door but no higher than up 3/4 of the door length.  Also, you want to place it so that it is VERY close to the other door, so that when the doors are closed, there is barely 1/8 inch between the other door and this lock.  Otherwise, anyone can get enough leverage to knock this off by pushing the other door.  When the lock is RIGHT UP AGAINST the other door when they are closed, not even I can push the doors so that it comes off!

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: This is the first product review I have written, but I really felt I needed to let people know about this product.  DO NOT buy this product unless you intend to modify it and screw it in the wall.  My attempts at installing it normally failed when it fell off with the slightest nudge.  I really needed it to work, so I drilled a hole in it and installed it to the wall with a screw.  With that modification, the product works well and is very sturdy.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: This product does NOT work.  It\'s very flimsy - my son was able to open the closet door after we put it on because it bends easily.  We ended up taking it off right away!!

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: Perfect fit  and is exactly as described. There were no surprises. I bought two of them for my kids tablets. Love it.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: I have two of these installed on sliding cabinet doors.  The doors are wood with a glossy melamine coating, and the locks have stayed securely stuck for over a year.  They are simple for an adult to use - use thumb and finger to push both tabs down at the same time, then slide door open.  As long as there is 1/8" or so of clearance between the doors, they will slide freely with the lock compressed between them.  Upon closing the doors, the lock\'s wings snap out again, and the doors are automatically locked - easy!  Our son (now 23 months) has not put great effort in trying to defeat the lock, but I think it would be physically very difficult for a child his age to do so.  He could easily apply the pressure necessary to press the wing down, but to maintain that pressure on both wings while simultaneously opening the door is a tall order for a toddler.On the flip side, while investigating the lock one day, he pulled down hard on the top wing, and it snapped right off.  He went right over to our other cabinet, and snapped the top wing off the lock on that one.  He hasn\'t yet tried to break off the bottom wings, and I believe that would be more difficult to do, but I docked this product a star for the easily-broken plastic.  It was fully effective until age 23 months, I haven\'t found any alternatives that are as convenient as this, and for the time being, it remains effective even with one broken wing, so it still gets four stars.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: The sticky back didn\'t stick to my wooden closet doors. So I had to to screw them into the doors. They work great now though. I don\'t know what you do if you had to use them on a glass door. Maybe they would stick better to glass though

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: The first one fell off 48 hours after installation. It had never even been used because I left it unlocked while the adhesive set. The 2nd one fell off in less than 96 hours. It had been used once, but didn\'t fall off then. It was several hours later while we were eating dinner. No one was anywhere near it.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: We have had these locks for over a year, and it is just now wearing out.  If you have more than a 1/2 inch gap in between your closet doors, these may not work for you.  We have vinyl-over-wood (so it looks like fake wood) closet doors and it sticks great, be sure to clean the area thoroughly like the instructions say, and our adhesive worked well.  But my son never forcefully tried to open the door, he tried a couple of times, and gave up.  We are only now having to replace it because the plastic wing has broken off, but it\'s after over a year of heavy use!  I\'m willing to pay $3 more bucks for that long of wear!

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: Not much protection. You get what you pay for. Not secure for kids over 3.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: I can rate this product high because it serves the purpose in which I intended to use it. I wish I can say how well it works to keep babies or small children out of the closets but I can\'t. The purpose of these items are to keep my cats our of the closets. Yes, my cats are capable of opening the wooden closet doors and like to sleep or hide in there. Unfortunately, they leave hair everywhere inside and on my clothes. One cat became ill with stomach problems and left a mess on the floor and near my dress shoes. Therefore, I had to put a stop to this soon. I then found these locks which stick very very well and are currently going strong after a month or so since I purchased them. Therefore, even if you don\'t have small children to keep safe, you can also use these for your pets. I love the locks...and of course, my pets.

name: Sliding Door Locks
review: Got these to keep our 21mo old out of the pantry and the cat out of the linen closet. The one on the linen closet has stayed on. But the one on the pantry popped off after about 4 days of my son trying to open the door. I put it back up using 2 3M Command Strips and haven\'t had any problems. If I need to use the others I bought on the doors in the bedrooms I will def use the 3M adhesive first!

name: Basic Comfort Seat Back Protector
review: This product might workout for other states but I live in Phoenix Arizona and thought this would be a great idea for scuff marks not!! The adhesive part to stick to your back of the seat because of the heat kept the back from staying on to the seat. So now there is no adhesive left and they just hang on the car and pretty much are worthless not a good investment for the Valley of Sun.

name: Basic Comfort Seat Back Protector
review: I purchased a set of these for my new VW Jetta with cloth seats - the velcro does not stay at all - and the ties didnt line up with my headreasts - so they were VERY UNUSEFUL to me - I ended up throwing them away.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: I love being able to pump, store, and freeze milk right in the bottle I\'ll be using to feed my baby. They fit the classic Avent bottles and the new natural style.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: I loved having all of the accessories that allowed me to pump and store breast milk directly in Avent bottles even though I didn\'t have an Avent Breast Pump.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: excellent product, very good quality, arrived in very good condition, 100% recommended a comprehensive kit for the pricemy baby loves his bottles ...

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: These made my newborn kit complete. Great for storage, no leaks. You can also write the date on them. Easy to use.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: If you are breastfeeding and using Avent bottles, these are a must! No longer do my bottles tip over and leak in between work and home. Plus you can stack the bottles in the fridge, so they take up less space. Also saves on the number of nipples you have to buy. I wish they were easier to find in my area, but thank goodness for amazon! :)

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: This was the perfect addition to our bottle collection. I\'m a breastfeeding mom who pumps for one bottle a day and am happy to be able to store milk in the fridge and then simply exchange these inserts for the nipple. Great purchase if you\'re using Avent bottles already. With that said, it advertizes that you can write on the lids... I\'m not really sure how one would do this (with what kind of pen) and be able to reuse.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: These really dont do anything special. I cant find a use for them. The AVENT bottles are a great way to waste your money. Shame on Philips for guilting people into buying AVENT products. There are many many many more products that will do the same thing for 1/5 the price

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: Having a newborn means that you live in world of disarray.  It also means that you are perpetually and endlessly washing bottles and making formula.  Half the time we can\'t find a nipple and just need to seal the bottle and get it in the fridge--ENTER these bottle sealing discs.They create a tight seal and pop in and out easily.  They will also prove useful later on if we want to use a bottle to hold cheerios or fruit loops:)

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: Works as expected. I use this with my extra bottles for storing pumped breast milk so that it can easily be warmed and served to baby.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: We love using the sealing discs for making bottles and mixing the formula.  They work wonders.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: These snap right into place and keep a secure seal. I use wet erase markers to mark the date on top. A good investment for added convenience.

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: very useful product. My baby feels good drinking in this bottle. I really like AVENT line, it\'s easy to clean and to have in good conditions

name: Philips AVENT BPA Free Classic Bottle Sealing Discs
review: I have Avent bottles, but not an Avent pump, so I did not get any storage bottles.
