review: Intially I was trying tobuy convertible seat good from 5 -40 lb. But preice of infant seat and infant to 40 lb is same . I like quality of fiber and ease of setting seat in and taking it out .

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: When I was pregnant, I saw this carseat and knew that it was the one I had to have. I liked how the print didn\'t seem to favor one sex. Most of the seats in the store are blue or have little animals all over it (I\'m not big on those animal prints.) Anyway, my daughter is now 4 months old and I haven\'t had a problem yet. I love the infant head insert. She just seems more snug and comfortable in it. And I absolutely love the big canopy. It\'s so much bigger than the rest. In response to those saying that the handle clicks too loud, just hold the parts in some so that when they snap into place, they don\'t click. Either way, my daughter is now used to the click it makes. Now I just can\'t wait to buy the 3-1 convertable carseat for her! :)

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: I have not used this product yet but am very interested in it.  This will be my first carseat for my first baby.  I have read a lot about the convenience of a carseat fitting into a stroller and wondered if this seat did the same for any EB strollers?If anyone has any suggestions on this or any other type of carseat for a newborn, I could use them.  Also, I looked at some of the infant/toddler (in one)carseats.  None of which sounded safe in my opinion.  Is it better to just purchase a new one when they grow out of the infant carseat?

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: My husband and I purchased this car seat because we were told by the salesman that the stroller would be out in a few weeks. We have since found out that you can only get the travel system and not just a stroller. We have seen the travel system and to be honest the car seat really stinks. If we the consumer are spending good money on a seat that we like why would you not sell a stroller seperate too, or at least the travel system with the nicer seat. Shame on you Cosco for putting out something that everyone likes and then not selling a stroller to match seperatly.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: overall this is a very attractive seat. my hubbie and i chose it because of the suede appearance. my 2 month old fits very comfortably and i especially appreciate the harness,which does not need to go over his head,and the canopy which pulls down quite far and has a vinyl window so he doesnt feel like hes in a cave. however, the seat weighs a ton and is about 25% larger than most seats. i wind up using it sans the base because its very akward lifting it high enough into the back seat of an suv to snap it in. i have to climb in every time to use the lap belt to secure it. alternately, it wont fit into our volvo sedan without the base to lift it some 5-6 inches off of the seat. for the price, id definitely buy this seat again.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: I was completely happy with my Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat.  I needed one because my new granddaughter was visiting from out of state.  The car seat looked nearly brand new.  It was easy to use and both the baby and her mother were pleased with it.  With the base in the car, we used the car seat both in the house and for travel safety.  Both baby and her mother were pleased with it.  We plan to use it for this baby, and for more grandchildren in the future.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: What I liked this item is:1. After going thru the other travel systems on display in the store, it was the easiest car-seat to pop in and out of the stroller;2. I liked the fabric patternThere are some things that really need to be improved about the seat:1. When you move the carrying handle into position, it clicks REALLY LOUD when it snaps into place and wakes up my baby everytime unless I squeeze the sides of the handle as I\'m lowering it.2. Latching the lower portion of the restraint (in-between the legs) is difficult because you have to line up the plastic pieces on each side of the strap like pieces of a puzzle just perfectly or it won\'t go into the latch---so, forget about doing this with one-hand.3. Unlatching the lower strap is difficult as you have to press REALLY HARD on the button to release it---again, you need 2 hands---one hand underneath the latch to give you leverage to push (so you\'re not crushing your baby\'s crotch area) and the other hand to push the button.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: I purchased this car seat for my daughter, my third child. It is wonderful. It has the built in head padding that keeps her tiny 6 week old head from flopping from side to side. It also matches my 2 year olds convertible car seat and the interior of my vehicle. This car seat also fits into the tandem stroller.I did not find the base to be any harder to install than other car seats( I do not have LATCH).Yes, the handle does make a loud noise but, my daughter has not been bothered by it for more than a second.Overall, it is a very sturdy car seat and I feel comfortable that my daughter is safe and secure in it wherever we go.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: At first glace this car seat is very appealing.  We bought because it was an Eddie Bauer and we really liked the pattern. We thought that buying an Eddie Bauer named product would be good quality, but we were wrong.  It is very very poorly constructed and the doesn\'t always lock into the base very well. The hood is poorly made and very flimsy.We decided to return it before our daughter was born and went with a Graco car seat and have been very pleased.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: The straps are hard to adjust, the buckle in the front hits my baby in the thighs (ouch) and does not adjust. It feels loos in my car.  Made VERY CHEAP.  I baught because of the looks, bad decision!

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: In answer to Lisa, about where to find.  We have only been able to find the double stroller in this pattern.  I\'ve scoured the web for any indication there is a single and have yet to locate it.  My husband loved this pattern and I figured if he finally got excited about something I should let him pick.  If you find a single let me know.  Otherwise the double one should be in your local babierus store.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: Just finished our registry and they now have this design in the single stroller travel system at Babies R us.  It is priced at $199.00

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: I only gave this car seat 1 star because I really don\'t like it, the only thing I do like is the print, it is classy, but everything else is terrible.  The car seat itself weighs about a hundred pounds, it is very uncomforatible to carry, the canopy thing never stays up and worst of all the straps keep coming undone, I believe this carseat should get rechecked by those safety people because those straps coming undone all the time is very dangerous.  If I could I would like my money back and as of today I am searching for a new car seat.

name: Eddie Bauer Infant Car Seat tan
review: I recently purchased the car seat and then I found out that it was going to be offered in a travel system. When the travel system was released I was so excited and I returned the car seat for the travel system. Even though the car seat that goes along with the travel system looks the same it is not. The car seat is not the same quality at all. The car seat that you buy individually is much nicer then the other. I am very disappointed in the travel system!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We looked into the Britix etc. and for the money - this is a great car seat. Our son is very comfortable, even on long rides.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: The seat is exactly what I was looking for.  It got great safety reviews.  I couldn\'t pass up the price!  It was shipped quickly.  It was easy to install and my son looks so comfortable in it.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My husband I and were debating over two similar carseats. (The other one was the Eddie Bauer 3-in-1.) We were particularly interested in the reclining feature and the 3-in-1 options. In the end, he chose the this carseat because of its color. Not the best determining factor, but of course we believed them both to be safe carseats.I am a stubborn person, not to mention impatient at times, and I put together ALL of our baby products once I was on maternity leave. (I even put the crib together when I was 8 1/2 months.) So I knew that when I had been struggling with this thing for 30 minutes, something was wrong.After on the phone with a representative of DJG for an HOUR, we came to the conclusion that the LATCH belt was too short. Even when we took the base off! This belt is so short that it doesn\'t even reach the front of the car seat. DJG\'s suggestion was to simply use the vehicle\'s belt, which I refuse to do since it pulls the side of the seat up.They will be sending me a new LATCH belt and a supervisor will be calling me by tomorrow. I will be sure to tell them that they need to ensure all car seats come with the proper equipment and are ready to go!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I just bought a second one of these. I bought the first 1 1/2 yrs. ago for my little girl and just bought the second for my youngest son. I\'ve been thru tons of car seats with my 6 kids over the years and this is my favorite. I was hesitant to spend so much money on one seat but hey, it goes up to 100lbs. so I guess the price isn\'t to bad. I\'m very glad now I spent the money. I read some other reviews on here where people said they can\'t get the seat level in the rear facing position, I\'ve never had that problem--I just stick a rolled up towel under the edge. I do agree with people about the size of it though, if you have a smaller car/truck this may not work for you. I drive a excursion and have no problem, I\'ve also put it in my husbands cougar but only in the forward facing position. I think the best thing I can say about this seat is that its VERY user frienly--my 15 yr. old can install it and put her sister in it with no problems. It\'s got a wide stable base, comfy padding, nice head support and easily adjustable straps. We\'ve traveled all over the west coast and mid-west with our daughter in one of these and she never complains!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I was looking for a car seat that my 14 mth old son could transition to. I was also looking for something that would be a one time purchase that could grow with him. I found this in the Cosco Elite. Car seat has plkenty of cushion for support, material is soft and durable. my son love the removable cup hold( makes him feel like a big boy).Overall this was a good buy

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I was in an accident this morning in which I hit a tree with the side of my van and then spun 270 degrees.  My toddler son, who was rear-facing in this seat, wasn\'t even shaken - though I think the van is totaled.  I will be ordering the exact same thing to replace that seat, now that it\'s been in an accident.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I\'ve read many of the reviews and don\'t know why so many people are having problems with the seat being backwards facing, or how the buckle works.My son is 4 months old and the seat is easy to get in and out of my Suzuki Grand Vitara and my Subaru Outback.Sure it\'s a tight fit in the Suzuki, but it fits.  If it was forward facing I\'d have no problem.Also, the leveling was easily adjust using a couple of Pool Noodles.Overall, I\'m happy with it, and my son is happy since he now has room to move his arms and play with things, something he could not do in a tight infants seat.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My husband and I purchased this seat for our son when he graduated to a front facing seat.  WE love it and HE loves it.  My son is very secure in this seat as well as comfortable.  The seat has been safe AND stylish for the last year and a half and has been easy (as carseats go) to clean...we\'ve had a few vomitous events in it.  We are purchasing a front facing car seat for my 1 year old daughter now and it will definitely be the Alpha Omega Elite.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: The Alpha Omega is quite possibly the worst product my wife and I have purchased for our baby, now 10 months old.  The only thing worst than an overly complex (horribly complex) and crappy product is two of them...and we made exactly that mistake.  My wife purchased one for her car and one for my car.The two primary reasons that product absolutely is the worst product we have purchased for our daughter are as follows:1) It is EXTREMELY to set up...this is a huge failing in the engineering and design.  It is easy to make a difficult and cumbersome product; it is challenging to create a well designed and easy / intuitive product.  It is VERY clear to me that the engineers that designed this monstrosity have never actually had to use it for their own families.2) You simply cannot remove the cover---in less than 1 hour.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: Not only was it a complete pain to install, the straps loosened up while I was driving and my 10 month old worked her way out of the shoulder harnesses.  In addition, it is TOO DIFFICULT to get my daughter buckled up - it takes so long to get the complicated buckle to latch that the last time I used it (before I returned it) someone in the parking lot actually ended up helping me buckle it!  So it wasn\'t just my imagination - even they said I should return it!DO NOT BUY THIS CARSEAT!  I did only  so we would be saving money in the long run and it ended up wasting time and energy instead.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I purchased my first alpha omega when my nephew was 6 months old - he is now 4 years old and I have had his seat as rear facing, forward facing and now as a booster.  My last minivan had a bench seat in the second row so his seat took up about the same amount of room as his infant carrier.  My current minivan has captains chairs so it just fits perfectly - his baby sister\'s infant seat takes up more room.  She is now almost 7 months old and getting ready for an upgrade into a bigger seat.  I am getting her her own alpha omega because I just love this seat.  For me, it is the easiest seat to get into my vehicle - her\'s will have LATCH which will make it even quicker to install.  My first one does not have LATCH, but I can get it installed in less than 5 minutes.These seats are large for cars that have small backseats, ie BMW 3 & 5 series, Jeep Cherokees, older Toyota Corolla\'s, and 1997-2000 Dodge Stratus & Plymouth Breeze.  These are all vehicles that I have had to put my nephews seat into and it is a very tight fit.  Two seats would be pushing it in these vehicles.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I bought this seat and spent an hour trying to install it in the rear facing position. I tried it with the latch and with the seat belt and either way the seat still moved around and would not stay reclined. I took it back the next day and bought the Britax Roundabout, installed it in about 5 minutes and it is very stable and comfortable for my 5 month old son.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I bought this seat because I wanted one that lasted from infant to booster.  We bought it when my son was 3 months old.  He\'s 20 months old now, and I called the manufacturer for a refund.  First, the base of the carseat broke.  I was annoyed, but I called Dorel and they said it is safe to use with or without the base, forward or rear facing.  Then the plastic on top where you adjust the headrest broke, so the bars to adjust the headrest started falling out all the time.  Then two weeks later I took the cover off to wash it and noticed the plastic buckle at the crotch was cracked all the way through!!!  There is no way this seat would have lasted several years like I wanted it to.  And I just used it like a normal car seat, it\'s not like I was throwing it around or something.....  Other than falling apart, it was a nice and comfortable car seat while it lasted.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I could not install this seat securely in TWO of our cars with flat, normal seats. I\'m not a car seat novice........I tried every trick. After over an hour, I gave up. Seats aren\'t safe if they aren\'t installed correctly, and I have no faith I could install this seat correctly.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I was in an extremely bad car wreck in November 2005. My car flipped over 4 times and we landed upside down. My [...] was strapped into his car seat in the middle of the backseat. The only thing he had was a few bruises from where car seat held him in place. I honestly feel that had he been in another carseat he may have been seriously injured! I received a broken femur from the crash.I purchased the exact same car seat again!! I would not put my child in anything else!!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I researched car seats until I was literally in tears when I was pregnant with my son and registering at Babies R Us.  I was so afraid of choosing the wrong seat! I read Baby Bargains and every on-line review I could find of as many car seats as possible.  I am happy to say I\'m so pleased with this car seat.  It fits great in my \'04 Yukon behind the passenger seat (second row seats are not bench style so no middle seat)and while we did not use the LATCH, it\'s buckled in so tight, it doesn\'t move at all.  My son is super comfy (moved him to this seat when he was 4 mos old) and likes to put his arms on the arm rest. The cup holder is the right size for his straw cups, and I honestly have never had trouble with the straps or the latch.  We originally had the Alpha Omega (not the Elite) and those straps drove me insane - they were always twisted.  But, the car that was installed in was involved in an accident and we replaced the seat with the Elite (my son was not in the car when it was in the accident but the insurance company said we needed to replace the seat anyway)and the straps on this have not been a problem at all. And as far as the latch goes, I\'m glad it\'s a little puzzle piece.  My son works on that thing and has not been able to open it at all.  I\'m not sure that would be the case with a different style latch.  When the seat was rear facing, I took it to be inspected and found out we had installed it incorrectly. They removed the base and used a pool noodle to get the recline right - we had read the manual and watched the video and still couldn\'t install it right, so I would definitely recommend having the seat installed.  Forward facing was MUCH easier.  I know my son is safe in this seat and I am glad this is the one we chose.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: First - let me say that I purchased the Britax Wizard because I feel it is the safest seat on the market.  However, I have to rebut what I believe are exaggerated and alarmist comments by karenbest1969, the fireman "expert."  True, Consumer Reports stated "...Cosco Alpha Omega 22-150 convertible seat were structurally damaged in our crash tests ...", but for whatever reason he/she left off the second part of the sentence "... although both restrained the test dummy adequately."  Furthermore the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ... rates the Alpha Omega 22-150 an "A" or "B" for securing the child in both the rear and forward facing modes.  They do rate the product "C" in the booster mode.The Britax is a pricey selection, and one that not all can afford.  Per the NHTSA and CR, I interpret the data to show that the Alpha Omega 22-150 is a safe choice at the lower price point.  If one states EMT or fireman credentials, let\'s be sure to give the public all the facts.  Yours truly -- Dad of Zach, Army Ranger!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I love this seat.  My daughter was 4 weeks when I bought it she is 6 months now.  We havent had a problem yet.  Yes you have to use something under it to fit properly.  I would recommend the car seat leveler.  It works great my seat dosent move at all.  When installed properly (I installed this myself was not hard) it does take up alot of room.  To solve that you install in the middle of the back seat.  Which is the safest place for baby.  My husband has a F150 crew cab and I have a ford escape (a very very small SUV) and it fits fine in both rear facing.  My daughters head stays back when she sleeps. I love that you can tighten staps from the front.  The buckel is tricky when you first try it but then becomes a breeze.  I think this seat is worth buying you only have to buy one and your done.  I would rather buy a seat leveler then another car seat.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have 3, yes 3 of these seats.  I needed to buy one for each car my baby rides in because these car seats (and car seats in general) are too difficult to transfer between vehicles. I like this seat but I don\'t love it, thus the 3 stars.  I was attracted to this seat because it is forward AND rear facing, it converts to a booster seat and will hold toddlers up to 100 lbs.  I did a lot of research and ultimately decided on this seat, despite some negative aspects. But this car seat is definitely not for everyone.Problem 1: In the rear-facing position this seat is HUGE.  The seat fits ok in the center seat of my large SUV, but did not sit well in the center seat of my Grand Prix, which is a fairly decent sized car.  It hit the front seats and wouldn\'t recline enough.  Unable to drive with the seat up too much, we moved the car seat to the rear passenger side.  (Not quite as safe but my baby infrequently rides in this vehicle).  It reclines fine now, but the front seat is up so far, nobody can comfortably sit in the front passenger seat.  It does fit ok in the center of the Oldsmobile Aurora, which is about the same size car as the Grand Prix, but the seats seem to be shaped differently so that the heardrest part of the car seat sqeezes between the two front seats. This seat (rear-facing)would not fit well in smaller cars.Problem 2:  The seat (rear-facing) is supposed to recline so that it is level with the ground (there is an indicator level line on the seat).  In all 3 vehciles the seat isn\'t close to level despite being fully reclined so we are forced to stick towels underneath to prop it up.  The instructions actually recommend this course of action which I initially didn\'t think would be safe.  The seats don\'t seem to move so I\'m not concerned, but it is still a pain.  If the seat isn\'t reclined enough, my baby\'s head hangs forward and looks uncomfortable. (We discovered this when one of the front seats was moved back, pushing the carseat into a more upright position - not good)! Also, after a while the towels shift and the seat needs to be reinstalled.  If the seat is loose, it\'s not safe for baby.Problem 3: I think that the harness is easy to use.  I have no problem securing my baby in and taking him out, but the straps do occasionally get twisted and untwisting them can be time consuming.Despite its problems, I bought 3 of these seats because they were nicely padded, I like the armrests, they have nice high backs for tall babies, and the cup holder will be nice when he\'s older. I like that the strap is designed so that my baby won\'t be able to easily undo it.  And I love the fact that this seat will grow with my baby.  My baby, whose initial birth weight was under 7 lbs., outgrew his infant carrier by the time he turned 4 months because he was too tall.  Considering how quickly he was growing, and the number of carseats I need to buy, I didn\'t want to buy one that went to 40 lbs only to have to get another one that goes to 80 or 100 lbs a short time later.  For this reason, I\'m able to deal with some inconveniences (since none of them pose a safety concern) until the seats can be turned forward facing when my son is a year old.  I\'m going to love this seat when its forward facing.  But for those who aren\'t willing to deal with these inconveniences, you may want to find a different carseat.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My daughter will be 3 in July, and we\'ve had this seat for her since she was 6 months old and outgrew her traditional "baby bucket." We have had NO problems with this seat. It is a BIG carseat, but latches in easily, takes less than 5 minutes to completely strip down, washes well, and re-assembly is a breeze! We\'ve never had any problems with the straps getting twisted, and you will LOVE how easy it is to adjust as your child grows. This is one of the best and more comfortable seats on the market. It\'s roomy for the kids, so they don\'t feel all squashed in (I have a friend who\'s 3 year old is outgrowing their almost 300 dollar Britax and is now uncomfortable in it) and it has nice padding. I don\'t have one bad thing to say about this carseat! We have a 4 month old, and she\'s getting her own Alpha Omega Elite here in just a few months! We love it!Heather

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This is a nice carseat, but the straps twist up all the time. What a pain! Our $40.00 carseat from Target is so much better. Just an FYI shop around before putting this on your list.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I just bought this car seat for my 8 month old son.  I have a 1997 honda civic, and for a compact car, I think it fits just fine in the rear facing position.  My father installed it for us, and yes, it did take alot of time.  If you install it properly it should be fine.  If it is not right, I would suggest to go to the police station to see if it is installed properly. Apparently, everyone has their own opinions, but I think it is so much easier to put him right in that than the infant carrier that was so heavy for me.  I love it! Good luck!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: Do not buy this item. My baby got a huge scratch(more like a cut, since it bled) all the way across the side of his neck from the belt. It was hard to install. Also it would not stay in the reclining position, and the baby\'s head would fall forward. Also it was annoying to lock him in his seat. You had to clip the two pieces of the belts together like a puzzle piece and then keep them together while you stuck it in the buckle. Very annoying. My baby hated being in the seat. He would cry before I even put him in and he would get very upset. It was horrible. After his neck got the big scratch and cut, I ripped it out of our SUV and returned it. I had done a lot of research and had planned to buy the Britax Marathon, but the representative at Toys R Us told me that the Alpha Omega was wonderful and great for the price and that it would last longer. Well I am so happy I returned it. Now I have a Britax Marathon and he loves it. He doesn\'t complain when I put him in. It is so comfortable and so easy to lock him in. I hope this review helps people. Your child is worth the extra money for the Britax. I know mine is. I am so glad that I returned it. I gave Babies R Us the picture of what happened to my babies\'s neck. They said it was good that I returned it and they also asked if they could keep the picture. I said yeah, they can send it to Cosco, because Cosco has lost my business forever!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I purchased this seat almost 2 years ago for my then 6 month old son.  When I purchased it is was missing the LATCH system.  I called the co. and they overnighted them to me.  The seat takes up a lot of room (especially when rear facing). I have a Infiniti I-30 and am not able to put it in the center it had to be placed on the side.The only problem that I have had is it is difficult to take apart to clean the seat.  With a 2 1/2 year old (potty training) it is a pain!  But I think I would have the same issue with any car seat.  My son loves it.  It is comfortable and living in south Louisiana it is not too hot like the thicker seats!  I would recommend it and will probably purchase another just like it when I have a second child.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We are very satisfied with this car seat.  We have 3 car seats by this brand name.  All have worked well.  No complaints.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have the Cosco Alpha Omega car seat from 2002 for my son who is now almost 3. (I drive a 2002 Chrystler Town and Country). I heard that this carseat is not good for rear facing because you have a hard time seeing your baby over the seat, So I bought it when he was 1 and I love it. I bought a latch strap to make it more secure (both lower and top anchors). My husband, (who can bench 345 lbs) can hardly get this seat to budge. The seat is placed in the middle bench behind driver. Having the pull strap in the front makes it easy to adjust the harness for what ever my son is wearing. The puzzle latch was easy for me to get, it took my mother-in-law some training before she got it but I love that it\'s more secure that way. I had to clean it the first time when we he got sick five times driving home from Oregon on vacation. Fairly easy to take apart and reasemble (not everthing can be velcro or easy snaps. Those don\'t always stay on when you want them to). I am looking to buy this one for my daughter who turns 1 this July. I\'m sure it will be as great or better as the one I already have.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: At 4 months old my son was to big for his <22lb infant seat.  On a budget and wanting a seat that will grow with him, we pick this one.  We have a Chevy Blazer and it is a snug fit, but my son is very comfortable it.  Guaranteed to put him to sleep.  We just had to put a towel under the back side of it to make it recline better.  It is very easy to get him in and out.  Best of all it goes up to 100lbs.  With the next baby we will go staight to this car seat.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We at first bought a cheap $30 car seat and it was horrible. This car seat is well worth the money. We didn\'t buy it until are daughter was 8 months old so I\'m not sure how it works with a newborn but my daughter loves it!! So comfy she falls alseep in it and her head doesn\'t drop down like it did in the other car seat. I drive a minivan so I have no problem with it fitting. It only takes up one of the bucket seats in the back. AWESOME!!!!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: As a mother of two small babies and aunt to 3 who I keep every afternoon, I never have less than 3-4 carseats in my car at one time.  We purchased this seat for my now 2 year old and my sister bought it for her 15 month old.  I read many reviews saying how bulky this seat is and I have found just the opposite.  I recently purchased a Graco for my 7 month old and it is much bulkier than this seat.  Any convertible carseat that can be forward facing and rear facing will be bulkier when facing the rear of the car mainly due to the recline... that\'s math:)  I love this carseat and am so pleased with my purchase.  The only think that I do have trouble with is the straps twisting on me. This is why I give it 4 stars... that bugs me so much.  When you remove the padding to clean the seat you can easily straighten them out though.  I was also pleased to see that you can wash the straps in the washing machine.  Many carseats have attached straps and they get so dirty after time.  I used this seat rear facing and now front facing and have no complaints at all.  It\'s really the best for your money and the best overall seat that I have found.  Good luck finding one that works for you and I hope this has helped!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I really like this carseat.  I just bought it and it works great for me. Very nice carseat for the  price.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This car seat is really a pain.  First of all the lower buckle is so difficult to attach when baby is wiggling and screaming!!  Second, my straps keep twisting!!  We chose this car seat based on looks and price...but I would much rather pay more money for the Britax.  We will be returning this carseat tomorrow!!!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have owned numerous car seats made by Graco, Century, and Cosco; and I have to admit that this is, by far, the one I like the most. I purchased this car seat for my daughter (now 23 months old) when she was about 5 months old. I drive a \'97 Chevy Blazer and a \'03 Pontiac Montana and had no problem installing it rear-facing, nor did I have any problems getting to the recline or belt-adjusting latches. I have only encountered the "strap twisting" problem a few of times, but it is quite easy to untwist them (in less than 30 seconds). My daughter was in a hip brace for 4 months, with no problem getting her buckled in correctly. She was also in a full body (SPICA) cast for 3 months, and with the strap extended to full length she fit perfectly still. This is one of only a couple of car seats that can be used for babies with a SPICA cast. My other daughter (age almost 5) has also used this car seat as a forward facing car seat and booster. It was very easy to change the strap height adjustment without having to redo the straps. The infant headrest came out very easily once we didn\'t need it anymore, and I did not find that it was too big even for the baby at 5 and 6 months old...All that I can say about this car seat is that for our family it has been the best purchase we have ever made!!! Once we read the instructions and watched the video, it was very easy to work this seat. No complaints here at all, We love this seat!!! Will never buy a different car seat.!!!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My daughter has been in this seat since she was 8 mo. old, she will be 2 in 17 days - This seat is awesome!  It fits perfectly in my \'03 Corolla - I cannot beleive it does not fit in SUV\'s as said in the other reviews... This seat is great, my daughter loves the arm rests and cup holder!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: im very happy with this carseat. it has everything that i need in it and its very easy to clean and looks very comfortable. we had an older version of the omega elite that had a overhead where you down and just click which worked great but when our daughter got older she learned how to get out of it every time no matter much i tighten the straps so i went shopping for a new carseat and found this one it had good and bad reviews and seems like everyone was complaining about the size of this carseat.  truthfully i think its just perfect. i drive a chevy avalanche and it is just the right size for it. granted if we had to make it rearfacing it would be too big but i dont think that any carseat that is convertable would fit nicely unless you drive a mini van. plus my daughter loves the feature with the cup holder. and most importantly it keeps her in her carseat now and she cant figure out how to get of of this one since its a 5 point and you have to unbuckle two instead of one. so i think this is a great one and i have a 1 month old now and once he gets old enough or he gets to be 20 lbs then im buying another one.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This car seat SEEMS to have everything that you would want--longevity, comfort, price...but such is not the case.The straps are VERY DIFFICULT to tighten while the seat is rear-facing.  I had to pull the slack from behind the seat in order to get my daughter safely in the seat.(She is 11 months and 21 pounds)  Why should I have to do this and how would I go about it once the seat is forward-facing?The straps also twist constantly making an already frustrating situation worse.I thought I must be doing something wrong until yesterday when I could not get the buckles into the lock! The lock was clicked as if the buckles were allready in except that they were not in! I had to fool with it for a long time to "unclick" it so that it would accept the buckles. (Yes, the puzzle pieces were fit together properly-that was not the problem) Without the harness fully locked, this is useless as a SAFETY seat.  It is going back to the store today.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: after carefully doing hours of research on car seats i choose this one. i read other peoples reviews and thought that they weren\'t doing something right. the bottom buckle is like a puzzle peice and when your baby is crying and kicking it\'s near impossible to get to together. the straps twist too easy and although it\'s not hard to untwist it\'s just one extra thing i don\'t have time for. my son is 4 months old and looks smushed in it. the recline doesn\'t recline as much as you\'d expect.  the strap you pull to tighten the  harness is near impossible to tug. refacing it hits the back of the seat and you can\'t pull up on it only out and the seat is in the way. but even with no seat it still doesn\'t tighten enough for my 4 months old. maybe it would be ok for a 1 yr. old and forward facing but it still needs a lot of time to figure out and adjust. im returning it and playing with every seat out there before i buy another one.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have bought many carseats for my 17 month old daughter. Our first convertible seat was a Graco Comfortsport which I hated. We live far from family and go on many long trips and when she fell asleep her head would hang forward. This does not happen with the Alpha Omega. She looks so comfortable when she\'s sleeping. Also, the seat fits great in my small SUV (Ford Escape). Yes, it is a big larger than some other convertible seats, but I like the fact that it is bigger and more "sturdy".  I think bigger in this case means safer. I have seen that many people complain about the straps twisting, but we have had this seat for a few months now and I have not had them twist even once. I think if you\'re careful and observant when you take your child in and out you will not have a problem. To me, most straps in most carseats are the same. If you are not careful any of them can twist. Overall I LOVE this seat and it was definitely worth the money.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I think I have given this seat the ultimate test. We bought this seat for my daughter when she became too big for the infant carrier. She has been usuing it for 2 years. It has been wonderful. We even went on a very long road trip to Disney and she was very comfortable and slept well for the entire 26 hour ride there and back. We liked it so much we just bought 2 more for our second daughter (one for each car) We are even making the trip to Disney again. I am not worried about the comfort and safety of my children in these seats. We have them installed by our local fire department and have never had a problem with that. I will say that it is difficult to clean in the event of  a sick child. I had to take the entire seat out and shower it off in the tub and air dry it outside. However, I can\'t imagin that this is something that is easy and enjoyable with ANY car seat.  I would recommend this car seat !!!!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I bought this car seat after both seeing  the "four and a half" star" customer rating and then reading all of the GLOWING reviews that past customers had written.  I based my opinion on things that were posted on this site about the ease, convenience, safety and customer satisfaction that other parents were writting about.  I HATE, HATE, HATE, HATE this car seat!!!!!!There is nothing easy about having to pull this car seat COMPLETELY apart when you need to wash it.  My daughter is 14 months old and vomitted on herself today in the car so I had to literally tear this car seat apart to clean it up.  I called two seperate Babies R Us stores to speak w/ someone about this car seat and neither of the people I spoke w/ knew anything about customer service and nobody could give me a bit of help or information about getting this monstrosity of a car seat pulled apart.I consulted my manual several times, but that didn\'t clarify anything either.  It was very cumbersome, ackward and difficult to pull this seat apart just to simply wash the cover.  I don\'t know who designed this car seat, but obviously my guess would be someone sadistic who has no children.I will NOT recommend this car seat to ANYONE ever! Not even someone I don\'t like, this car seat is a cruel joke and a complete and total waste of money that would have been better spent on a simpler, better and more simplistically designed!!!!!!!  This thing is completely awful!I hate this car seat, think it is a complete waste money and would NEVER recommend it to anyone looking for something easy, convenient and just simple to pull apart to clean!  Never again will I purchase anything made by Cosco!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I really hate this car seat. It takes up way too much room. The only place we could fit it rear-facing and securely was behind the passenger seat. To do so we had to shove the passenger seat all the way forward so that means there is no room any longer for a front passenger. And even then the seat isn\'t reclined as much as the indicator says it should be (almost but not quite). I would have never purchased this seat. My mother bought it without consulting me and I used it because I\'m broke. I have an incredibly small car and this is the worst seat for it. If I had an Escalade maybe there would be room. This thing is HUGE. Besides that it\'s difficult to get the baby in and out and adjust the straps. There is just nothing good about this thing.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: In the fall of 2003 I was in a horrible head-on collision.  I was 8 months pregant and traveling with my 17 month old son.  This car seat was wonderful ... so wonderful that I have two more now.  AND I am dreading the day my kids outgrow the seats ... My son is tall for his age and may outgrow the seat before we get to use the booster (my one complaint).The emergency workers were not only amazed by my son walking away from the accident with only one scratch (from a toy hitting him), but they were amazed that the seat was installed properly and that we were using it correctly.My children are now 18 months and almost 3 years old.  Both are in the Alpha Omega seats ... both since they outgrew the Snug Ride.  We have had no trouble out of either of the seats.  We have them inspected every 6 months to make sure they\'re still installed properly and that the kids are still buckled in correctly.I read some of the other reviews and one complaint was the infants head was forward ... then the seat was not at the 45 degree angle.  Anytime you install your seat, you should have it inspected and learn the proper way to install (especially if you trade out seats between vehicles).  [...] can help you find a location near you for inspection.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This car seat does have a bad smell.  I took all the covers off and washed it and it still smelled, but it has pretty much aired out over the last 3 months that I\'ve had it.  The covers are extremely hard to take off for washing.  As far as the safety of it, I really feel like my daughter is safe in it.  I have leather seats and I\'ve had other car seats slide around, but this one stays put.  She seems comfortable in it too.  Overall I like the car seat, but washing is a HUGE pain!  The safety and comfort for my daughter are what matters most to me, and I feel like this car seat provides those two things.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My son is 6 1/2 months old, and just grew out of his Graco Quatro Tour, which I loved so much. So we bought the Alpha Omega.  My husband installed it, and it was pretty easy.  We have a Subaru Outback, and the car seat doesn\'t seem to fit in the car properly, it doesn\'t recline to the right degree. So whenever he is sleeping in the car, his head falls forward. Also the material of the seat collects any sort of dust or fuzz, which is annoying.  The car seat is nice, and it is also convienent that you never have to go out and buy another one.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We registered for one of these almost three years ago when my first son was born.  When we had our second son, we prucahsed another. Now both boys sit in this seat and we are thrilled.  One is rear facing and we do not have to use towels (We have a Chevy Impala) and the other is forward facing but on the slight recline.  Neither of our sons heads fall when they sleep and we feel VERY secure having our children in these seats.  Our oldest seat has the buckle that must be laid over the other but the new one is simple.  You put either side in then the other.  I couldn\'t ask for anything better in a seat!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have not yet put my son in this seat.  I just bought it today.  It did take a while to get the latch belts in the way that are supposed to be.  And come to find out they didn\'t even secure the seat in my Honda Pilot.  The carseat moved all over.  I had to push the passenger seat almost all the way up into the dash to get the seat to fit in the rear facing position. Also, if using a seatbelt to secure it is a pain to have to take off seat pads and put them back once seat is in place.  Maybe now that all of the initial setup is done it will work out great for my little one.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have recently purchased this item and I was very unhappy about the product.  I  had to return it the next day due to the buckle not being able to unbuckle and the positon against my daughters thigh cut across her thigh and ended up snapping her thigh and leaving a bruise.  There was no way to adjust this and make it work for her.  It was to loose in the cheast allowing her arms to get out and to tight against her thighs.  My daughter is 1 year and in the 65% for her wieght and hight so that wasn\'t the cause.  I wouldn\'t recommened this product to anyone that cares about their child

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I have a 2 year old and a very large 6 month old to transport and the ease of adjusting the carseats is a must.  This is the easiest car seat to adjust and the most comfortable for my kids.  We go on long car rides and have never had a problem with the seats.  It may be a little more pricey but for the range of weights that it works with it is by far the most reasonable we could find.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I dont understand how anyone can give this car seat 5 stars...The thing is huge and bulky!!  I have an Eddie Bauer Ford Explorer, and this car seat takes up almost half the backseat and makes it difficult for someone to sit in the passenger seat.When installing it in the rear facing position, it is not sturdy AT ALL!!  you have to recline it so far back (the reason the front passenger is all scrunched up), and still my daughter does not look comfortable.It took forever trying to get the latch system right, since the manual is so basic. The only thing that helped me is by reading the Ford manual and understanding how the LATCH worked.The cover is very difficult to remove and put back on..I cant imagine removing it over and over again to wash it, its a nightmare...You are supposed to be able to recline the car seat with one hand, yeah sure, use 2 hands and your knee to hold the seat down to recline it...THIS CAR seat sucks so much i\'m returning it tomorrow and getting a Britax....and for all you know it alls out there, please dont even try to tell me I dont know how to read a manual or follow directions, This is the only review I have ever written because everything else I own does not SUCK as much as this car seat does.GOod luck if you decide to try it...waste of money...luckily mine was a gift and I will exchange it for one that is better.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I\'ve tried 2 others but this one is the one! It\'s comfortable, easy to use, very sturdy and safe. Definitely worth the money.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I started using this carseat for my son when he was about 9 mths old.  I loved it at first, even in the rear-facing position, but now I\'m not as thrilled with it.  My son is now 16 mths old and is average size.  I can pull as hard as possible but one of the straps just never gets tight enough.  I had this issue once before and my husband fiddled around with it to get it tight again.  How many times do I have to do this when this was supposed to be a very safe car seat!  It\'s not safe if the straps are not tight enough. We have the Evenflo Comfort Touch carseat in my husbands truck....now I wish I got 2!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: After having an infant seat for awhile(birth to 11months) for my child, I decided it was time to shop for another carseat. I decided to purchase this one because it can go up to 100lbs.Prior to installing, I read the directions.The directions are NOT user-friendly. It took me forever to figure it out. When I did install it, it was pretty simple. The directions and diagrams are terrible.It did fit into my OLDs-Intrigue with no problem. We are using it rear-facing in the middle. I do notice that her head slouches down when she is sleeping and the carseat is reclined to the fullest!I would not suggest this carseat for an infant. If my 11 month old, 19.5lb baby\'s head slouches over when sleeping, imagine a newborn. Other than that my infant is comfy in it.Oh I almost forgot! This carseat is wonderful because it has the head brace so your infant\'s head won\'t be move to much around. Just in case you get into an accident.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This is a great car seat.  After we bought the 1st for my 7 month old, we liked it so much, we replaced our 2 year old\'s car seat with this one as well.  I\'m not sure why others are having a hard time installing this car seat, unless they have never installed one before.  If it takes you 3 hours, you obviously haven\'t a clue, and should go to the CHP, and have them install for you in 5 minutes.  It took me about 10-15 minutes to install this rear facing in a 2002 Sonata w/ latch.  It was no harder or easier than any of the other car seats I have installed.  The seat is well cushioned and the belts don\'t twist as easily as some others.  BTW, the belts can tighted plenty, and the buckles are ingenious and easy to use as are other Cosco car seats.  I really can\'t understand the reviews people give based on one day with the car seat.  My 2 year old likes it AND it keeps her very safe.  What more do you want?  All in all, a great seat!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We use this car seat for our 2 year old daughter and it seems to fit snuggley in any car we use it in. I love it and so does Emma.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: The thought of multi-purpose anything is wonderful, but this is not what I had in mind.  I really don\'t recommend this to anyone who does not own a mini-van.  I say this because the seat takes up alot of space and this goes for those tall people who needs the extra leg room.  The chair isn\'t angled low enough like an infant chair, so my son it very uncomfortable.  I also had a friends toddler seat in it for a ride and it was ok~ until he feel asleep.  There wasn\'t enough padding for his head so his head would swing like an ostrich.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: Overall this has been a very good carseat.  I bought the Alpha Omega based on all the good reviews it got.  We bought it when my son was outgrowing his infant carrier carseat.  We did not have bad problems with the straps twisting like some of the reviewers claim.  It transitioned nicely from a rear-facing seat to a forward-facing carseat.  However it claims to last and that it can used as a booster seat with only the lap belt.  I was hoping to use this seat until my son was big enough for just the lap belt, then I would go out and get something like the TurboBooster.  My son is now 2 years old but only 25 pounds, so I can\'t use only the lapbelt.  The Alpha Omega (at least the one we own) has only one set of holes for the 5 point harness straps to come out, so they can not be adjusted anymore.  Since my son\'s shoulders are now above where those holes are, the straps constantly slide down off his shoulders.  We will have to go out and get a booster seat that has a 5 point harness.  It\'s a good, comfortable seat, but if you really want one to last, make sure there are at least 2 holes for the 5 point harness so that you can adjust it as your child grows taller.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: We bought this shortly after my first child turned one and I love it. The fact that you only need to buy one carseat is a added bonus. I live in california and we have the carseat law 8 years 80 pounds and this carseat will take him all the way threw. We are now expecting our seconed child and am planning on buying the carseats for both my car and my husbands. I drive a Dodge grand caravan and it fits well on the smaller of the two bench seats as well as the captians chairs. My husband drives a 74 dodge challenger and the carseat fits well with the added teather strap attachment for a forward faceing postion( not needed in the caravan).

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I purchased two of these car seats over a year ago for my twins. I agree that in the rear facing position the seat takes up too much room and crowds the front seat. It is also a bit wide, if you have two you can\'t put them side by side which makes it hard to get to the third row of seats. .We travel to Alabama about every 6 months. It\'s about a 12 hour drive straight through. In our old seats my twins cried for the last 6 hours of the trip and when we arrived they both had pressure spots on their bottoms. This is after stopping every two hours for them to walk around and play outside for at least 15 min. So our trip actually ended up taking almost 15 hours. Riding in a car for long periods is hard but if you have uncomfortable babies it UNBEARABLE!My twins have taken 2 trips in these seats.  Not once did either child fuss about being uncomfortable. We only had to stop 3 times and that was to eat, get gas and change diapers.I have taken the covers off their seats 4 times and is not that hard to take off or reassemble. After washing they look new, no fading or pilling.Overall it is the best and the safest on the market and I think it was a well spent $350.00.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I\'ve had an alpha omega for 3 years and love it.  Its great because it can be used from 5-80 lbs.  For the reviewer that said he has no room when the child is rearfacing - that is true for every rear facing seat I\'ve seen.  The puzzle clasp is designed so that the kid can\'t get out which is great b/c my child can buckle the top but there\'s no way she can do the bottom lock which makes it more secure

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: This seat is terrible for rear facing. It will not recline the way it should even if you put your front seat up to your dashboard! It takes forever to install because you have to put it together and adjust everything before you even attach it to your car! The instructions are not very clear either. The puzzle buckle on the five point harness is a terrible pain with a wiggling baby and has very sharp edges that can scratch your babies legs for sure! After one day of trying and watching my five month old sons head bob when he fell asleep I took it back and bought the Triumph by Evenflo. It took about five minutes to install because it comes fully assembled and it fits in the proper recline position even with my SUV\'s seat all the way back! It is easier to get baby in and out too without any scary looking sharp edged puzzle buckle to hassle with. It just has a normal five point harness. Save yourself the hassle and do not buy this for a rear facing seat!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: My 21 month old son & I were recently in a head on collision while he was seated in this car seat.  The officer on call, and my doctor, said that thanks to a lot of luck, my car and this car seat, little Billy only sustained a few scratches (from the little matchbox cars he was holding) even though the car was totaled.  I was injured more even with the airbags and my seatbelt.  I am going to buy this seat again.  I firmly believe that it saved his life, and after all that is it\'s real purpose.  In addition - on the day to day use, I found him to be very comfortable and getting him in and out was fairly easy. My only complaint about this seat is that it faded quickly.  I will say that I never used it as an infant seat, actually when I registered for this seat I never intended for it to be anything more than the toddler seat. I find the "bucket" seats to be much easier as an infant.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I thought this seat would solve my delima with a tall baby. My child is long and lanky. Not Thick at all, and it rubbed his neck RAW! The pads moved out of the way and the straps are too close together. Also, his head flops fwd, like the other reviews have said.I had to return the seat, after 5mths use. The end of the line with it, was trying to put it in a friends van! It was sitting straight UP! I have it rear facing as he has Just turned 9mths old. We took a 2 hour road trip, and he was miserable, and that is when the straps hurt him. I would be afraid, VERY afraid if an accident had occured! DON\'T Buy this seat!

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: First of all, I have not used this seat rearfacing ever. I purchased it once my daughter outgrew the seat that was part of a travel system. I love this carseat, and she does as well. I was recently rearended and pushed into another car (at high speed) and my daughter was ok, not a mark on her. I am going to buy her the same seat again now. The old one still looks perfecty fine (we\'ve had it for 2 yrs) but after the wreck I am of course replacing it. The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is that the latch system hooks on this model (which are the same for the Graco Nautilus) are just very basic hooks and one of them bent soon after we got the seat and is somewhat of a hassle to remove. So, for forward facing use in only one car, where you are not inteding to switch the seat out a lot, it\'s a great choice in my opinion. One more note: when I first bought the seat, I thought I could use the recline for making her more comfortable on long rides to sleep but it is not to be used forward facing, unless you need to recline it to level it correctly.

name: Cosco Alpha Omega Elite Convertible Car Seat
review: I think this car seat is one of the best.  When we were looking to find a toddler car sear for our daughter we couldn\'t decide on this one or the Britax.  They were comparable in safety and features.  This one is so so easy to adjust for height and comfy.  She always falls asleep in it.  Not to mention the price was a lot better.  I do however wish that there was diffirent cool covers like what the britax has like leopard print.

name: All Stars - Mobile
review: I purchased this mobile to match my grandson\'s decor.  After using it 10 times it no longer turns or plays music.  It\'s a shame that you are charged 39.99 for a piece of junk.

name: All Stars - Mobile
review: The mobile was not at all difficult to put together, as I read from one customer.  I put it together in less than 10 minutes, and I had no problems with anything breaking.  I just can\'t rate its use any higher because my son isn\'t born yet, so I haven\'t used it besides the one test wind I did to hear the song.  It fit on the crib just fine and it is adjustable.

name: Baby Calendar
review: I really wanted to like this, but found it a time consuming hassle to organise the photos, hand draw bits of it, prepare each month\'s photo, duplicate photos in case of loss or damage, write out instuctions and text for each month on the form and on the backs of the photos, etc etc and send it all off to then wait for it to be printed and returned to me.There are a lot of things you can do if you can be bothered with a big arty project but it\'s much simpler (and cheaper) to upload your photos to Walmart Photo or Walgreens, edit and organise right on your computer at home and order your calendar through them.I am quite an \'arty\' person but this all seemed a bit time consuming. If you are a busy Mom like me this may not be the way to get a lovely keepsake for yourself or a gift for family members. I have been very impressed with the variety of photo gifts that can be ordered through Walmart and it seems to be a much easier. quicker, simpler way to get a lovely personal calendar keepsake.

name: Lambs & Ivy All Stars Decorative Throw Pillow
review: This is so cute and goes great with the bedding but it is spot clean only.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: This set is very pretty and the price is reasonable compared to others.  It\'s a very girly-girl set and the colors work well together.  I only really have two negatives:  first, the sheet is paper-thin and rips easily b/c it doesn\'t fit over our standard size mattress.  Secondly, the bumper only has ties on the top and not the bottom which I think would be much better.  Other sets out there have on top AND bottom.  I think it\'s safer.The quilt is very plush and can be used on the floor during tummy-time.  However, one side is very decorative and I worry about a child being able to pull the ribbon or tulle off and possibly choking.  I only put my baby on the plain, striped side of the quilt.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: I adored this set.  But after washing the set a second time, the corner of the sheet was completely ripped apart.  I am afraid to wash any of it again.  I read the reviews for the matching toddler set and they all agreed to poor quality.  I am going to check with the company to see what they will do about it.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: This is the prettiest crib bedding I have ever seen and BRU has some gorgeous sets. I had narrowed it down to Gossamer Wings until I saw this one. I knew instantly I had to get La Petite Bebe for my baby girl and I\'m so glad I did. The diaper stacker ties in the front with 2 little bows and at the top there is a pink crown with a heart in the middle and the words "little princess" above. The bumper also has this design at the headboard and at the foot of the crib the bumper has a little pink heart covered with white lace. The sides have flowers, ballet slippers and a hat box accented with real bows that my daughter loves to reach up and touch. The window valance and dust ruffle are varying shades and sizes of light green stripes so the room isn\'t overdone in baby themes, but is still very cute. The sheet is white with a pattern of pink daisies and dots and the quilt has beautiful details stitched into each square. It has the same as the bumpers in addition to a star which says "a star is born", a pink tutu with a real crinoline skirt, and a big fluffy French poodle. Each design has a different texture which makes every square stand out. This bedding set turns a baby girl\'s crib into a little priness\'s palace.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: This bedding is absolutely beautiful and I love it. However, here is a tip if you are on a budget, don\'t buy a bedding set. I found, all you really need is crib sheets, a bumper, and a blanket to keep baby warm. Although really adorable, I found the quilt useless. So, if money is not a concern, get this.. but if it is.. you probably wont use the quilt.. or atleast I didn\'t.. So you can get everything separately and save some cash..if u decide to get this i purchased wendy bellisimo\'s sir leapsalot wall art.. the one with the two froggies and that looks beautiful with this set.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: I HAD NOT BOUGHT ANY NEW BEDDING WHEN I FOUND OUT I WAS PREGNANT WITH MY SECOND CHILD BECAUSE WE DIDN\'T FIND OUT WHAT WE WERE HAVING.  I HAD LOOKED AT A FEW DIFFERENT STYLES OF BEDDING FOR EITHER BOY OR GIRL AND WAS REALLY HOPING I WOULD HAVE A GIRL SO I COULD USE THIS AWESOME LOOKING BEDDING.  IT IS REALLY "GIRLY GIRL" AND FEATURES PRINCESS AND BALLET AND A LOT OF PINK.  AFTER HAVING MY GIRL I PURCHASED THE BEDDING WHICH IS SO CUTE AND I HAVE HAD A LOT OF COMMENTS ON.THE ONLY THING I HAVE A PROBLEM WITH IS THE SHEETS.  I ENDED UP GETTING THE SHEET THE SET COMES WITH AND 2 ADDITIONAL.  WITHIN THE FIRST FEW TIMES OF USING THEM THEY ALL HAD RIPPED BECAUSE THEY DON\'T FIT THE CRIB MATTERESS CORRECTLY.  I WAS STILL ABLE TO USE THEM BECAUSE THE RIP WASN\'T UP TO WEAR THE BABY SLEEPS - BUT AFTER SOME MORE WASHINGS AND USINGS I HAD TO THROW THEM OUT BECAUSE THEY WERE REALLY BAD.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: My husband and I picked this out for our little girl to be, whom is due in a month.  It is just lovely and very girly but not overkill with the pink.  My husband was the one who just had to have this for "his" little girl! I think it will look wonderful in her room!

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: I received this as a gift in my baby shower.  Everyone that comes into my little girl\'s nursery ohh\'s and ahh\'s over how gorgeous the bedding and the matching ensemble is.  It\'s girly without looking like it was dipped in pepto-bismol.  The sage touches really set it apart from the rest; the tutus and crowns are just so delicate and feminine!The value is really great too, you get lots of pieces (others usually come with just 4 and cost more) The valance looks really pretty and I highly recommend getting the matching pieces (mobile, wall border, lamp, and definitely the wall hangings)The only problem that I had with this was the crib sheet, it\'s too small for the standard-size Sealy mattress that we bought for our baby --I think it\'s a manufacturing defect (someone in that company didn\'t measure the fabric correctly)  Luckily, I also received tons of crib sheets, mostly in different shades of pink, and a couple of sage ones, and they all look great, like they came with the setTo save yourself a tiny inconvenience, be sure to reinforce the bumper ties, one of them came off, but that was quickly solved with this little remedy called needle & thread :-)

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: We bought this for our 3 daughter last year and I couldn\'t wait to put it on her crib.  Well the very first time I put the sheet on her mattress it ripped!  I had to buy an additional sheet, I bought a solid knit jersey one instead.  The ties on the bumper eventually do fall off so you have to either sew them back or remove the bumper.  The valance I\'ve never used.  Would I spend that much on a bedding set again - nope.  Not worth it.  Its a cute set but the money spent is not the quality that you should be getting.

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: After 4 years of buying nothing but little boy items (which I do love!!) when we found out we are expecting a little girl, my husband and I went princess/pink crazy!!  I knew that I didn\'t want her room to be gawdy though (as so many princess themes seem to be), so we decided to stick with a Pooh theme for her bedroom.  That was until I actually went shopping.  When my girlfriend and I were at BRU to purchase the crib, this set was actually on the display of the crib that we purchased.  It was too perfect!  The green helps to mute the pink colors, and all the designs keep it just girly enough.  Since she will be staying in our room for the first few months, the colors flow nicely with the bedding on our full size as well.  Pictures are great; if you are able, go see this set live and in person as well...you won\'t be dissapointed!

name: La Petite Bebe 6 Piece Bedding Set
review: This being my first child and a girl, I really wanted to make her nursery a little girl\'s dream. When I saw this bedding set online I knew this was the one. Not only do you get the complete bedding set, including the dust ruffle, but you also get the window valance and the diaper stacker!!! What a deal for the price considering that most quality bedding sets only come with the comforter and sheets for the same price as the La Petite Bebe bedding. When the set arrived I was so excited, the bedding screams quality. You can see it everywhere, not just on first visual inspection but in the design and the construction! We also ordered the wall border, which matches perfectly with the bedding sets. Sometimes the border color and bedding colors vary slightly but these colors are an exact match!! My daughter is a dream come true and so is her nursery with the addition of La Petite Bebe bedding!!! I highly recommend this bedding set!

name: The Original STOKKE KinderZeat - rosewood
review: Expensive but really worth it.  Chair is very stable, and looks like "furniture," instead of cheap kid plastic junk.  Assembly required, but it is very easy to put together.  Our son loves the chair--wish we\'d bought it for his older sister years ago!

name: The Original STOKKE KinderZeat - cherry
review: MOST EXCELLENT FOR BABY OR CHILD:A remote Denmark co-worker OF MINE told me that much of Europe uses this chair.  I\'ve purchased 2 Stokke\'s for my grandboys - both grands love these chairs.  I love these chairs.  First, I love the sleek Euro style of the chair.  Next, I love that this chair allows seating&foot; support adjustments so baby/child can sit close to a dinner table and use dinnerware(baby or regular) on the table like the rest of the child\'s family (this is a good thing).  Child is close to family while sitting at table, while observing how dinner happens with family.  The adjustable seat & foot rests are made to work with the height of your child, providing ergonomic support for little body parts.  The chairs are stackable and can be moved to a corner or can remain at the dinner table. There are optional seat covers (or make your own for your dinning décor), an optional attachable eating tray for those who can\'t get USED TO NOT having a highchair tray-  but i would not purchase this if i were u.  My older grandson uses his chair at the computer for proper sitting. and the adjustable seat&foot; rests allows proper seating at any desk or work table for child activities. This was absolutely an excellent purchase for my grands which can be used up to ELEVEN years old - or by recommended top height- which ever comes first. This Euro design is superior to US baby highchairs and you continue to use this chair for many years to come.  It will be the only baby/child chair you will purchase, the good quality wood will allow this chair to be passed down to many little family members in the future.  A MOST EXCELLENT PURCHASE.  Get away from the old US baby highchair concept. It will be WELL WORTH IT!!!

name: The Original STOKKE KinderZeat - cherry
review: I recently purchased this "booster seat" for my now 19 month old.I have a "funny" story into how I wound up with a KinderZeat in my kitchen. I origionally purchased a cooshie booster soley on reccomenation, and it wound up ruining the finish on one of my brand new wooden kitchen chairs! I was devistated, I had to buy another chair, and a booster. My friend told me she saw this chair at BRU and thought I should check it out. I wound up purchasing it, and its probablly the most used item in our house.My son can get onto it himself, using the footrest as a step, like a ladder. He sits right up at the table, and doesnt use the harness. The seat adjusts for different ages/sizes, and even I love sitting on it. We made him a SpiderMan cushion for it, and he loves it even more. Its super easy to clean, and you can take it apart for easy storage.So, I wouldnt really have spent all that money for a booster seat, but now that I DO own one, I fully anticipate purchasing one after my now 6 week old uses and outgrows the Eddie Bauer chair we own. Ohh yea, this is NOT a highchair, and I think 12-18 months is a good estimate of when a child should begin to use one. Even with padding and a seatbelt, theres no sides, no tray, no full back. If money is an issue (we do not have the money to purchase another one really) then I have some solutions(1) Buy a highchair and then sell it on Ebay when your done, use the money to buy the KinderZeat (we will probably do this, but you still will need to add in money for it)(2) Borrow a friends highchair and then buy the KinderZeat(3) Purchase a cheap booster (like the healthy care) and then buy a KinderZeat(4) Register for the KinderZeat, and buy a cheap highchair!(5) Refrain giving your child solids until 18 months old (thats a joke)All in all some how we are going to purchase a second kinderzeat in a year or so, and put a kitchen chair into storage. Boy, if I was rich my whole house (and the houses of everyone I know!) would be furnished with these chairs, they match my decor, and are easy to clean. Kids love them, and they are timeless. A perfect booster for decades.

name: The Original STOKKE KinderZeat - cherry
review: We purchased one for our son when he was two and just ordered one for our 18 month old daughter.  We have another kid on the way and plan to order another when he/she is around that age.  No messing with booster seats, phone books, or sitting on his knees.  Reduces spills and wiggling because he is at the proper height.  VERY easy to clean - sponge, cloth, or dust buster and voila, all clean!  We even took our kinderzeat to my parents when we visited.

name: Stokke Natural Tripp Trapp Chair
review: We already owned one, just wanted to pick up another for the next kid.  It\'s great.  If you can get one, do it.

name: Stokke Natural Tripp Trapp Chair
review: Bought this chair over a year ago. Thought it was the most attractive highchair on the market. And "Wow! She\'ll use it for years! Maybe she\'ll even use it as her desk chair when she\'s studying in college!" Loved it up until this morning, when we had to call 911 after she pushed herself over backward (and was semi-unresponsive) in the chair. If you have hardwood floors, it works just fine...it slides back easily. We just moved to a house with rough stone floors and it does not slide at all (even after putting flet "sliders" underneath), therefore it tips backward with little effort. I hope you take this into consideration if you have stone or carpeted floors. Now I\'ll be looking for a chair with a tray.

name: Stokke Natural Tripp Trapp Chair
review: This was a great solution for my grand daughter who was 2 and refusing to sit in her high chair any longer.  Having her sit on her knees on a table chair was not safe.  She gladly sits in her new chair at the table and is much safer.

name: Stokke Natural Tripp Trapp Chair
review: We got a hand-me-down Stokke for our then 4-month-old but could have used it sooner.  As soon as she learned how to she enjoyed being able to climb in and out herself, something no other high-chair I know will allow a kid to do safely.Tripp Trapp sell baby trays, but they do not mount on the chair.  Instead, get thePlay Tray for the Stokke Tripp Trapp High Chair- not a Stokke product, but just as good - which has a easy to clean surface, a no-spill edge and is easily installed and taken off again.In Denmark the Stokke chair is a must-have for its simple, sturdy design and unmatched usability.  Our relatives\' kids use them still at age 10-12, I like sitting in it myself and we will get one for our new baby.

name: Stokke Natural Tripp Trapp Chair
review: I purchased one of these in 1979 for my first born. All my children used it and to this day I still own it and use it as an extra chair at the table for guest.  When they state "that it grows with your child", they are right on the money. I have given these as gifts to other parents and they too have loved them.  You money is very well spent on this product. Worth every penny.Nancy O\'Brien - Elmhurt, IL

name: Boppy Noggin NEST Head Support, Denim
review: This item really works.. The back of our baby\'s head was very flat. It has rounded out nicely since we started using this pillow about 6 weeks ago.

name: Boppy Noggin NEST Head Support, Denim
review: The product worked fine per say. The problem was that we took our son to a specialist for some flatness on the back of his head (four months old). We showed the noggin nest to him and after looking at it a couple of minutes he said he felt it was good marketing but shouldn\'t be used. He said that any surface on which the baby\'s head lies, becomes firm with the weight of his own head and therefore contributes to the flatness. And with the way our son would turn his head and lay in one position in his car seat, it\'s true that it still ends up being just another surface. He also said that given that his flat spot was due to him favoring one position, it would be important to not cradle his head straight, rather help him move it the other direction to loosen up the muscles. Both our specialist and our physical therapist strongly recommended not using this product. Instead, just lots of tummy time has helped him already.Along the same lines, they also said that boppy seats and exersaucers should NOT be used because they deter babies from developing proper back and neck strength.

name: Boppy Noggin NEST Head Support, Denim
review: Just get one of these (actually, I got two so I wouldn\'t have to keep moving it around so much.) At 2 months, our baby\'s head was getting awfully flat. Enough so that the pediatrician scheduled an appt at 3 months to look at it & possibly talk about "the helmet." I freaked & ran to our local BRU that same day. I used it in the swing, the activity rocker, the bouncer & in her stroller, but not her car seat. I also let her (danger danger!!) sleep on it at occassional naps. If I was sitting in my bed reading, I\'d lay her next to me on her noggin nest for a nap. (Nothing dangerous there.) I wouldn\'t let her sleep on it at night, or anytime she wouldn\'t be constantly supervised. At any rate, by 3 months, the doctor said she had improved immensely, we\'d just keep an eye on it. We kept using it & at 4 months, he said we didn\'t even need to worry about it anymore.
