I haven\'t taken this to use at a restaurant yet so can\'t speak to portabilty, etc. But it is pretty compact and easy to use so I can\'t imagine it would be too difficult. And my 6-month loves sitting up in it and banging on the table tray - yay! It appears to be safe and sturdy, even when he lunges to one side, it stays put (he\'s 20 lbs.). All in, a good deal.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My girl was very antsy sitting in the restaurant wooden chairs, and it seemed to be because she was sitting on hard wood, with a hard wooden back.  (actually, she was too small for the back to fit, so it was like stadium, backless seating for her).  This thing is great!  I\'ve ordered a second one for Grandma\'s house.  It is small enough to take on the go, it is easy to use and clena, and she stays still in it for a LOT longer.... making restaurant meals much more pleasant for everyone around.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: we are tight for space so this seat is great. It just sits on a chair and we don\'t need to have a clumsy highchair in our small eating area.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We\'ve had this chair for 5 years and through 2 kids and soon to be a third.  We knew we needed something to save space and we wanted our child to really be part of family dinner time when we had our first son.  We strapped this on a typical wooden chair and used it as a high chair for a while when I needed to plop stuff on his tray.  I\'ve always hand washed the part that clips on to the chair because it would take up my whole dishwasher.  The part that comes off would go through the dishwasher sometimes.  That was a pain in the butt when my kids got old enough they could pop it off and at that point I would just use the tray-my parents bought another one that set on and it made a HUGE mess with them flinging food everywhere because it was easier to get off from the time they were just starting solids.  We used it up to the table from the time my boys were around a year old each and they felt like they were part of the family instead of most kids that are in a high chair and shoved away from the table.  We\'ve used this on short trips, at diners, etc besides just our home.  It\'s very easy to clean and very easy to transport and adjust to a new chair.  The only thing that doesn\'t clean super well are the straps-those are a bit stained but that\'s to be expected.  After 5 years it still looks pretty new and we still use it every day.  We even use it as a chair to boost our kids up so I can cut their hair.  I would not recommend any other like product-this really is the best out there and we\'ve used several and different friends\' homes and family\'s homes.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have used this for both my kids.  LOVE IT!  Portable, sturdy and dishwasher safe (I think), at least I do it.  Only thing, it is hard to clean the straps.  Haven\'t figured that out well yet.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is a great seat and very functional.It is too small for my two years old, but, is nice, easy to carry and well built.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Before we bought this booster seat my husband and I would find ourselves struggling to feed our 8 month old daughter on our laps while we were out at friends houses, etc.  This seat is so easy and portable that we leave it in our trunk and bring with us to restaurants, etc.  My daughter loves it as well.  Buy this...it\'s worth every penny.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We own two of these ~ one at our house and one at my parent\'s house.  It is perfectly portable ~ we\'ve taken it to a football banquet and a Thanksgiving dinner, I just didn\'t want to take it on an airplane.  We are using it instead of a high chair to save space ~ it will grow with our daughter and I expect we will get a lot of years out of it.  It was highly recommended by friends as well.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We purchased the booster seat for our 9-month grandaughter for her visits to our home.  The seat is everything is said it would be at a very affordable price.  It is easy to set up and take down to store.  It is easy to clean.  We like the fact that the tray can go in the dishwasher and be disinfected.  Plus if my daughter would need to travel with the baby, it folds up very conveniently and they could use it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought the booster seat for a 5 month old who sits with assistance/support. I had three main considerations:1) I did not want to invest in buying a fancy high chair that has an option for infants to use it for just a couple of months but was concerned the baby will not be comfortable in this one.2) I looked for a chair that occupies minimal space by either folding or fitting under the dinning table3) I wanted something that is easy to keep clean.This booster is great in all of these three aspects and at times even exceeded my expectations:1) The baby is stable. We did put a folded blanket at the side of the chair to make the fit better. And I love the fact that this chair will continue to be used up until she sits at the table on a regular chair. Great investment! She likes the chair and gets tiered of sitting only near the end of the feeding session.2) The use of the two straps (one around the seat and one around the back of the chair) make it stable on the chair. It is low enough to be able to move the chair with the booster under the dinning table. So it takes minimal space and allows the baby to sit at the dinner table with the family, which makes feeding so much more fun.3) Cleaning-wise it is just wonderful -- easy to wipe off plastic that can be taken apart and thrown into the dishwasher.The only downside: You cannot put the baby in when the table compartment is attached to the chair. So you have to remove it and put it back in once the baby sits there. Its is not hard to do, but it is an annoying extra step to take, sometimes with a hungry or a fussy baby. Plus, I thought the whole point of a removable try is that you dont have to take off the whole table compartment for cleaning -- only the insert. But in reality you need to take them both anyways, so what\'s the point?!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: It is easy to use, easy to carry, easy to set up, and easy to clean.  The only down side is that my son very quickly learned how to reach forward and disconnect the grey and green tray attachments.  Now his meals are served on the blue base tray which he cannot detach.  However, this does make clean up a little more difficult.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this for my son because he will be starting on foods in a month. I wanted a high chair that is a space saver style as well as easy to clean. This seat seems to be just what I wanted! My son has been sitting in it about once a day to get used to sitting with us at the table and he appears to enjoy it. He is 5 months old and a little small for the seat, but that is good as I hope to use it for quite a while. Also, cute colors!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We have a Peg Perego high chair that worked well for the first month or two of feedings at the table because it reclined which was helpful at the start of feedings, but we have found that this, affordable, light weight, portable chair is the best all around. In fact, we like it so much, that we have one at each grandparent\'s house and keep one in the car for use when dinning out in addition to the one we use daily at home. It is easy to tote around though, so one will suffice, but for convenience sake, we found having a few a real convenience. We can also use the extras when other kids visit.The seat secures easily with two adjustable nylon straps and clips--one below a chair\'s bottom and the other around the back of your chair. We\'ve used it on a variety of chair styles and it has always worked. The seat is simple and contoured for baby\'s bottom and legs and the entire seat has 3 easily adjustable height setting so that baby can truly pull right up to the table with the rest of the family (note, the seat must be removed from the chair it\'s on to make this adjustment, but it\'s rare that you have to change it, as the size of the child determines the best height, not so much the table or chair height.) The baby is secured in the seat by a 3-point harness made of the same adjustable nylon and clips.The tray is simple to put on and remove. It simply clicks onto 1 of 3 nubs along the side of the arm rests. The tray has 3 parts--a base, insert, and cover. The base attaches to the chair and we use it for every meal. The removable divided insert is ideal for messy meals as you can remove it, clean it off, and even throw it in the dishwasher. Lastly, it has a cover that snaps into place on top. We don\'t use this at home, but it\'s handy when eating out to contain any mess left of the tray (or insert) until you can get home to clean it. The seat\'s lap straps can be poked back through the seat and taken out to be washed--a big plus, straps are so hard to clean are are always getting dirty.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I am the mother of 7 month old twin boys and that last thing I wanted was two huge highchairs in my kitchen. I researched this booster chair and listened to a review by another mother of twins and she was SO right.  This booster is a huge space saver,you can use any hard chair, and so easy to clean.  Three height settings will also come in handy as my children grow.  I highly recommend this chair - especially to a mother of multiples.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: The tray that you can take off is so helpful when trying to clean up after a meal. You can just take it away so the baby doesn\'t put his hands into the food after you\'ve already cleaned him off. The high chair is so transportable, it doesn\'t take up any extra room in the kitchen. We originally thought about getting a high chair from IKEA, but this is way better.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I purchased this for the smaller of my one year old twin granddaughters, the larger baby uses a high chair I was able to borrow from a friend. So in order for  little peanut to sit with the rest of us at a meal time-I purchased this. Shes fits in it perfectly fine, she is happy as all getup in it and to be part of the family at dinner. She will be getting weighed this week at her one year checkup, but I am estimating she is about 19 lbs and 29" tall. the entire set up cleans easily,  And since I never leave her unattended in anything-I wouldn\'t have the problems some of the other reviewers seem to have with the white tray pinching the childs fingers. I love the fact that it is height adjustable and the straps are long enough to fit around any chair in my house as well as my daughter & son in laws house. All in all a great booster seat. I would recommend this to anyone.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I got this for my son when he was turned 1 so he could join us at the table.  This seat is great, I wish I would have bought it sooner.  The only thing is the tray pops off too easy so my son was able to pop it off right from the begining. I only use it at the dinner table & I love that the height is so easy to adjust.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Love this little seat,  we use it at the table for the boost and also for snacks in front of the TV, since it has the cool tray!  Our Granddaughter loves HER seat, she treats it like my husband does his recliner!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My husband and I purchased this for our 7 month old daughter to use when dining out.  It is a great alternative to using the often dirty restaurant high chair.  We love how easy it is to transport, setup, and use.  Our daughter doesn\'t slide all over in it like she does in the restaurant high chairs.  Well worth the $$$.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is a very portable, nice-looking, and sturdy product. The buttons on the sides are not as convenient as some of the models that slide. I don\'t think we\'ve ever used the top tray cover (the green part) because 1) are you really going to put food on this tray, cover it up, and transport it? and 2) you\'re probably going to clean off the random chunky food bits before you take the thing home. My husband thinks it\'s great and preferred it to other snap-on models, however I feed our kid more and have to deal with its "quirks" on a more regular basis (i.e. he\'s been able to easily pull off the white middle tray by himself since he was able to sit up straight in it!), so my standards are a little higher. Bottom line: this is a good seat with a neat tray system and good height adjustment features, but the side buttons and tray stability leave much to be desired.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This item is very practical, good looking, and does everything it claims to do.  It was a good choice for us.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I just bought this booster seat for my 5 month old son. He is approx 27 inches long and about 16 pounds. We clip the tray to the middle spot. It is real easy to pack up and take with us. Very sturdy as well. Defiantly recommend!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Product arived fully assembled and easy you use.  We bought it for our visiting grandson, who is almost one year old.  Worked out great for him in lieu of a actual high chair.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This booster seat has several adjustments for the table to accommodate a growing child. The chair is easily secured to any existing dining chair with a seat belt from the back of the chair and from the bottom seat of the chair to prevent movement or slipping from the dining chair.  It also has a great seat belt system to secure our daughter in and the table locks into place easily and securely.  Any mess that our daughter makes, can be easily cleaned with a damp cloth/sponge. When the child outgrows the table attachment, the seat can become a booster to the dining table as well.  It is great, versatile and saves room.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We purchased this seat for our 7-month-old.  He fits in it well, with room to grow. It straps securely to the chair, even when he\'s moving.  The seat is easy to attach and easy to use when traveling.  The seat cleans up easily and the trays can go through the dishwasher.  Great seat for feeding a young child!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Cute and easy to secure to a kitchen chair! I bought it to replace a bulky high chair that was taking up space. We\'re using it as a booster and it\'s working great!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I purchase this after seeing a women at a restaurant with one. My daughter is turning four and we are just now transitioning out if it. At restaurants the tray allowed us to feed her without having to worry about crud, germ infested tabletops. For travel it folded small and was great to leave in the car for grandma\'s house. We then started to use it as a booster seat at home.  Of all baby items i have purchased this is the one that we used until the bitter end.  This is my first pick going forward for anyone whom is pregnant.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: These are great for my 18 month and now 2yr old twins at the dinner table,  but for us,  the extra trays are unnecessary though.  The babies just play with the extra trays while I prepare their foods &  they easily pull up on the sides of the entire tray & pull it off while feeding (total mess),  so the sides are a terrible design flaw &  too easy for a toddler to figure out.  So thats why I gave it 4 stars.  Otherwise easy to wipe up and clean (nothing but hard plastic and no crevasses). We have 2 Fisher price space saving high chairs that we leave upstairs in their room and feed them their bottles in those in the am and PM before bed.  The spacesaver has a cushion all around it for comfort and it has 3 recline positions (padding easy to wipe clean).  The tray on the space saver the babies can\'t take off by themselves.  Main reason we didn\'t buy more space savers for the dining room was because the booster is supposed to be more for toddlers that are ready to hop in &  out of their chair independently &  we felt they can grow into this one.  The booster takes up less room than the space saver (less bulk) & is easier to store.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is the only high chair we have used and it\'s great!  It is great for all of the reasons listed by others.  Plus our son seems to find it comfortable.The only downside so far is that it is completely made of plastic (not sure if any of it can be recycled?).  We wanted a wooden highchair (or something eco-friendly), but this is so much more convenient and affordable than anything else we saw.The best we can do now is take good care of it and pass it along when we are done.  Reduce, reuse, recycle!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I got this high chair as a baby shower gift (one I didn\'t ask for) for my first child and I was not super impressed at first.  Until I used it!  I recommend it to everyone looking for a high chair.Utility: It has a small footprint and sits on a regular dining room chair, strapped along the back and bottom of the chair for security.  As the baby grows into a toddler, the tray can be removed and it becomes a booster simply by sliding it up to the dining room table with the rest of the family.Cleaning:  One thing I found with this style versus a traditional high chair (which grandma has) is that there are far fewer places for food to cram itself into.  The tray removes and is dishwasher safe, which is very nice, but it cleans quickly and easily even in the sink.  The surface of the trays are smooth, with no joins, so there are no places for the food to hide.Portability:  I love how easy it is to carry around - the seat back folds down into the seat, and the tray is placed backwards on the latches.  There is a handle on the back, so you can carry this thing easily anyplace.Durability:  I like to tell people about the night we drove off with this seat on the roof of our car.  Pulling out quickly to get into traffic, we heard it fall off into the road.  It didn\'t get hit, but we were going about 20 mph when it fell off.  I was amazed to see that the only thing that happened to it was a big scuff mark on the corner of the seat where it hit the ground.  No cracks, no weakened plastic.When our second started solids, we bought another so both boys could have a seat.  I am now using that second seat with our fourth child, and we\'ve given the roadkill seat away.  But for the price, the Fisher Price Booster is worth every penny.  If I could tell you some negative things about it, I would, but I truly don\'t have any.  The only problem I\'ve had with the second seat in the past 5 years is that I set the seat down on the counter next to our glass-top stove, and didn\'t realize one of the straps was on a warm/hot burner that I had just turned off.  It melted the strap in half!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I think this seat is great as it really feels like you have a complete high chair with you once you attach it to the chair. It attaches very securely and the tray is great. It is easy to keep in the trunk and you can carry it into a restaurant or someone\'s house no problem and have it hooked up in a few seconds. I like the fact that I don\'t have to worry about what type of tables the place has as you do with the clip-on seats. You can also position the seat next to you as you would a normal high chair instead of being restricted to something attached to the table.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is really a deluxe, inexpensive little seat.  I really like how easy to clean it is.  There are choices for which way to use the tray, and a cover to keep it clean between uses.  Or, don\'t use the tray!  Pull the chair right up to the table so the child can sit with everyone else.  It makes feeding my granddaughter so easy.  It\'s also easy to take the tray off and unbuckle her.  Which I really appreciate when my arthritis is bad.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I love it, it\'s great and such a space saver instead of continuing to use the highchair in our small kitchen. I do wish there was more space between the chair and the tray. I think it sits a little low for my big guy, it is tight against his legs when I tried putting it on and it sits lower than looks convenient for eating off of. We always keep it pulled up to the kitchen table anyway and sometimes use the attached tray/plate on the table.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My 18 month old grandsons love sitting in it. Easy to clean as well.It is easy to take on the road.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: good to have when grand babies come to visit.  Could use some shoulder straps.  One less thing the parents have to pack.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this chair to use while traveling.  After returning home from vacation, I have stopped using our full size high chair and only use this one.  It is compact and therefore takes up less space in our apartment and it is much easier to clean!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: It\'s fine, what can I say? Haven\'t used any other so no idea what the industry standard is. My only complaints are really minor, not deal breakers but enough to wish on a rating star for.Good news:It appears durable enough, we\'ve been using it about a year now but only for travel, which we don\'t do all that often.The way it straps on to the back and bottom of a chair feels really secure.Easy to cleanI like that it includes a tray cover to keep the part they eat from clean when travelingWhat could be better:The "boost" doesn\'t go so high, could probably use a bit more height for short kids.The tray is kind of low when babies start to grow a bit, there\'s not a lot of space between the baby\'s thighs and the tray. My kid is even on the petite side. I realize part of the point of the booster is to raise the kid to reach the adult table, but sometimes you just don\'t want \'em there. But overall I imagine a heftier kid than mine would probably start to feel squished in this seat sooner than you\'d want.The inner (white) tray snaps off MUCH too easily. I was looking forward to having it both as a spare and to be able to easily bring it to the sink to rinse off, but instead I rarely use it and it\'s just an extra piece in the way because from the very beginning my 1-year-old could easily pry it off and send food flying. No good.And this is not a problem with the product, in fact it\'s exactly as described, but I just think people should know this is NOT a full high chair replacement. That would be the excellent "Space Saver" booster which I\'m about to review. But even though I didn\'t start my little one on table food until she was able to sit independently anyway, the seat of this booster was still not supportive enough for her at that point (I think she was about 9 months old when we first got this) - she was too little and wiggly and it just wasn\'t the same as high chair seats usually are more contoured. The tray is small too, which is perfect for travel and toddlers but not ideal for beginning eaters who don\'t yet understand how to keep their food in one place.Overall, this is an item that I\'m very happy to have in my car trunk, but for home I\'d probably get a more basic booster when my kid outgrows the high chair. The trays would be squashing her legs by that point and the boost isn\'t so high, I think most plainer seats would do the job very well or better for home. But for traveling with a baby to toddler, it\'s near perfect.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Omg! Great product great price. Our kitchen is to small for  high chair. This product is perfect.Well worth the money.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I purchased the Rainforest version of this chair for our second home.  I love it and would absolutely recommend it.My daughter loves to play with the toys and they keep her entertained while I am prepping her food.  We have taken it with us to restaurants and it is super easy to fold and take with you.  It\'s also very easy to wipe clean - no creases or other messy spots and it\'s not so darn big that it can\'t fit in the dishwasher!At home we have the Chicco Polly and I would definitely recommend this seat to a new mom over that one - not to mention it is so much less expensive.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Light, easy to transport (I move it often between the kitchen, dining room and patio), and good value. Eliminates need for a big, ugly highchair that takes up so much room and is bulky to move around.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My son was using the Safety First reclining infant seat which was great until he got to be around 9 months old and he HATED the high back of the seat, he was always banging his head on it.  Due to limited space in our house, I researched all the boosters out there and thought this one would be ideal as opposed to a highchair.The pros to this are:-EASY EASY EASY cleanup, no nooks, crannies, cracks or crevices for food to get stuck in.-Very portable and compact, easy to pack up and take to restaurant, Grandma\'s house, traveling, wherever.-High quality at very affordable price.However, there a few definite cons:-The dishwasher safe, removable plastic tray insert can be WAY TOO EASILY removed by an 11 month old.  I have spent more time cleaning his meals up off the floor than I care to think about.  I finally just stopped using the insert and just put his food on the tray.  A little more of a pain to clean that but at least I\'m not mopping daily.-The actual seat is VERY small and if your baby is even average size it won\'t last you very long.  My son is only 12 months old and he is already started to look absolutely ridiculous sitting in it and gets uncomfortable quickly.  He is 23 1/2 pounds, a little above average, but we put my friend\'s petite 1 year old in it and she even seemed uncomfortable.  I was hoping to use this booster until my son was ready to sit at the table in a regular chair but I don\'t think he\'ll be able to use it for much longer than a few more months.  I have no idea what I\'ll do at that point.So overall the seat would be perfect if it was a little wider and the tray insert wasn\'t so easy to remove.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This chair is great for a portable - folds easily down to take with you has a carry strap. Seems sturdy on the chair or table.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I am so glad I got this booster chair instead of a high chair.  It takes very little space and we always take it with us to my in-laws.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: If you have little space in your apartment for a highchair then you will be happy with this compact booster..

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This was one of the great "investments" we made in baby gear.  My sister-in-law had a Peg Perego highchair that she DESPISED!  They couldn\'t get it clean.  With their second child they switched to a booster seat and were never happier.  She convinced me to try a booster instead.  She is a smart cookie indeed!  We had registered for the Eddie Bauer wooden highchair because that was supposed to be so easy to clean, but (thankfully) we didn\'t get it.  I have a girlfriend who did, though, and she is completely jealous of my booster.I bought this particular item based on the reviews.  Everything people have said is true. I wipe it down quickly during the day, and give it a more thorough cleaning every night.  The plastic seat is contoured, and my daughter doesn\'t even notice that it\'s not padded.  She didn\'t start solid food until 5 1/2 months, and then we used her bouncer at first.  We never had a use for a reclining seat.  The 3 tray depth settings, 3 height settings, and the 3-point harness have given her plenty of room to grow.  The straps on the back and bottom are pretty long and have adjusted to every chair I\'ve ever tried with no problem.At first I used the removable tray insert, but realized that I was having to clean that and the actual tray anyway, so I stopped.  When my daughter was older I thought that a sectioned tray would be conveient, so I put it back on - once.  It took her about 2 seconds to flip it off.  So for me, this feature was completely unneccesary.I have not used it to go out to eat.  If we ever get to go to a restaurant again I may try it!  I did take it on vacation, and even though there were boosters there for the other kids, my girlfriends were using mine when I wasn\'t.I did not attach the booster to my regular dining chairs at home.  I had a pair of heavy wooden barstools with backs that we weren\'t using so I put it on one of them.  It definitely helps that we aren\'t leaning down to feed her.  I keep one of those thin cloth diapers (not the pre-folded) on the stool under the booster seat.  I brush off the crumbs and just switch it out with a clean one every few days.  If there\'s a heavy duty mess I replace it sooner.The only thing that I don\'t like is that food does end up in the webbing and clips of the 3-point harness.  However, I don\'t think there is a way around this on any product.  Besides, it\'s nothing a little scrub brush can\'t fix.  I\'m just the kind of person who wants to spend as little time as possible cleaning so I can maximize my time with my daughter!As an added bonus, I keep my barstool/booster combo in the kitchen near the back door.  Since the tray is usually in the dish drainer between meals, the seat is just sitting there.  When I am getting ready to go somewhere, I get my daughter ready and strap her into the seat.  It makes it easy to put on her shoes and gather up all the gear (purse, diaper bag, keys, etc.) before we walk out.  I\'m not chasing her around with an armload of stuff - or the opposite - holding her while trying to get my stuff together.The next baby is on the way.  I am buying another one of these seats and putting that other barstool to good use.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This was a great buy for our family.  I bought it one day on a whim and have been very happy with it.  My daughter had been using it since she was about 6 mos. old and she is now almost 2.  It shows hardly any signs of wear.  It is very easy to clean and has a very fast set-up and break-down.  We have traveled with it on an airplane and, although it\'s not what I consider compact, it\'s really light.  I plan to get rid of my daughter\'s highchair in the next month and switch to using this booster exclusively.  This is one product you will definitely get your money\'s worth out of!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We already had one of these given to us by my wife\'s mom.  Since our eldest was about 9 months old, we have been using it.  It is great!  Very durable and easy to clean.  On top of that, it\'s great for travelling.  We take it with us whenever we go on a road trip; fits easily in the car and straps onto any chair we\'ve tried so far.  We just got a second one for our youngest who is almost ready for it.  This is an absolute must if you take road trips with little ones and don\'t want to drag a highchair everywhere.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We have a small kitchen and a full size high chair didin\'t seem to fit anywhere. This highchair works great, even for my 4 month old who wasn\'t able to sit unassisited yet.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Fantastic value, great product!  We bought this to use with our 5 month old.  When we\'re not using it to feed her we put toys on the tray for her to play with.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This has been the best twenty bucks I have spent in recent memory. Lightweight, easy to clean and sturdy. Folds up perfectly. can\'t say enough good things about it!!! buy it

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I am so thrilled with this booster seat!  Not only is it easy to clean, but it looks good too!  I like that it has a few trays and a lid.  The funny thing is my 19 month old son loves it too.  When he knows it\'s time for a snack or meal, he walks right up to the chair and climbs right in.  Now he really is a part of the family during mealtime.  While standard high chairs are good, this booster takes up less room; my son is right there with us and the best thing is that there aren\'t any nooks and crannys that crumbs can find a home - clean up is minimal!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We absolutely love this booster seat! The best feature: It is so easy to clean. After several months of a full size Graco high chair with tons of crevices, cracks, and places for food to accumulate, I had about had it. 3 meals plus two snacks a day, and all I was ever doing was cleaning that high chair! We went on a trip to visit some family and bought this to take along. Small, secure, and a dishwasher safe tray that doesn\'t take up more room in the dishwasher than two plates would. When we got home, I gave that full size high chair one last good cleaning and then sold it! This booster was the way to go. Perfectly secure for a baby that is sitting up well. Easy to adjust straps for securing to chair. Takes up no more space at the table than a regular chair does. I don\'t see why anyone would use a full size high chair instead!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I wish that I had this chair when my other son was a baby. It makes my son more at ease to sit and eat at the table with us, doesn\'t take up any extra space and it\'s sturdy and holds up to the wrath of a baby :)

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I am glad we got this booster seat, it\'s convenient and much better than most high chairs in public.  My only complaint would be the slight difficulty in buckling the seat to chairs, you have to get down and reach under the chair to hook and tighten the strap.. which can be a chore when you have an active toddler to wrangle.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: What a great little chair for our one year old grandchild.  Our children have this chair in their home and we bought one before an upcoming visit from grandbaby.  It\'s easy to use and so easy to clean.  Our old wooden high chair didn\'t have a safety strap as good as this and it was a pain to clean.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Our baby loves getting fed in this chair. We also have a full sized Peg Perego high chair and even when we\'re home she prefers to eat from this wonderfully practical, portable chair. We are about to travel with her for the first time and this is definitely coming with us. It\'s easy to clean and put together. She also just loves playing with her toys on the tray. We\'ve already gotten our money\'s worth with this purchase.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have used this product for three children, two of them are currently using them. Highchairs are SO overrated and completely unnecessary. These are easy to clean, safe for children, and portable! When at someone else\'s house during a mealtime, I just take this seat and voila! No seating issues for children. This also works as a good chair for playtime activities such as coloring, or just as a seat.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: EASIEST TO FOLD! I went to the store and tried folding all of the travel boosters.  After getting frustrated with the cheaper brands, I figured this one out with no instructions!  I have friends with the cheaper brands, but this one is worth the extra five dollars.CLEAN!  I absolutely love the tray cover!!!! What a great idea.  My friends\' boosters do not have this.  My husband and I just returned home from a DC vacation.  Our son is 6 months old and he loves to lick everything in sight (and some things under the sofa:).  It was comforting to eat out with a clean surface for him to knaw!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My 6 1/2 month old granddaughter loves this chair.  Even when she\'s not eating, she loves to be up at the big table where she can see everyone.  The chair is very secure and appears to be very comfortable.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is the best booster ever, I\'m convinced.  I can put it in the dishwasher, and that alone, gives it so much appeal.  I\'ve had the same seat thru both my girls, and it\'s proved practically invincible thru them both :)  It\'s wonderful, it was the best $25 I ever spent, and I\'m so thankful to have it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Since we have a high table in our home, normal high chairs could not work for our baby. After searching and reading reviews, we chose this booster seat to be the main eating area for our child. It looked durable, clean and has a name we trust. Our baby began eating in it at 4 months and is now 8 months. Recently we have found bruises on her back and looked for the cause. Our child is not in daycare and is in our care all day. We realized that when she gets excited, she bounces up and down in her seat. The back of this booster seat is hard and is the reason she has these bruises on her back. We now place a small pillow behind her to solve this problem. I would caution any parent from buying this seat or any others without a padding on the back. No parent wants to see thier child harmed, especially if they know they could prevent it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: was a gift to give works  just what they say it will.. good construction and materials works  just what they say it will.. good construction and materials

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Every parent should have this.  This is one of the top 5 baby/toddler items that we have.  It stays in our car and we can bring it with us to restaurants and other people\'s houses and we don\'t have to worry about nasty high chairs or where the baby will sit to eat.  Love the cover for the tray, so while it stays in the car, the actual food tray keeps clean and free of dust.  And everything is super easy to wash. By far one of the best purchases we made!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought this for my granddaughter. Love it because there\'s no fabric and the mess is easily wiped up. Nothing to wash after she eats. Lovelies I can push my chair in under the table with it attached. Fits perfectly.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is a great traveling booster seat.  We have one for each Grandma\'s house.  Don\'t know what we\'d do without it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have an in home daycare.  I have tried several different boosters, and this is the best!  The best part is how easy to clean that it is.  Other boosters have cracks where food can build up.  They\'re a pain to take apart and clean.  But this one just requires an easy wipe down.  It\'s also easy to fold and carry with you.  I would definately recommend this booster seat!  I now have 3 of them.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have 3 children. I used a fisher-price healthy care deluxe booster seat with my oldest kid and used the "space-saver high chair" with my second kiddo because I had sold the other one when I had to move over-seas. I stuck with the space saver high chair but it was such a pain getting food stuck in the crevices and under the seat pad and not being able to pull all the way up to the table. I ended up selling it when I had my third child and buying another of the fisher-price seats. I\'m very happy I did. So much better. It\'s easy to clean and it can be used easily instead of a high chair with a 5+ month old in my opinion. And just for your knowledge; my almost 3 year old climbed up in the seat and closed the tray around him when I wasn\'t looking and he fit just fine. Highly recommended.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: it is so handy. we use it evey day. it cleans up very easily. we don\'t use the insert tray like we thought we would, my daughter kept pulling it out. but still very happy with it. it\'s compact enough we take it also when we travel to families houses for weekend trips and whatnot.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: i just love how convenient and easy this chair is to use for my 5 month old. we just started him on solids, and wanted a high chair that would be easy to take to grandmas house, and one that attached to a regular chair.i bought it because of the terrific price and good reviews and am not disappointed! love the plastic cover that you can put over the tray when you are not eating, to keep it clean.Its super easy to clean, baby seems comfortable in it, and when he gets older, we just pull it right up to the table and its a booster seat.probably the best all-in-one baby product that will last long into toddkerhood that i have purchased!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We\'ve been using this as a high chair for our kid since he was about 10 months old. He\'s now 19 months old, and we love this thing. Fits on one of our normal kitchen chairs (so no extra stuff in our kitchen dining area), holds him securely, and cleans up very easy. Just make sure you clean under the seat every so often, quite a lot of stuff ends up between this booster seat and the chair.Additionally, you can just take this thing with you when you go on vacation or even just to a friends house for dinner, very portable and sets up in seconds.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Just received this booster seat today. It fit perfectly on my bar height chair to my kitchen island.  Now my 21 month old Grandson can have breakfast or snacks with me at the counter instead of his high chair. This will also work great on my dining room chair when we have dinner.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I really love this chair, especially the color, which is why I bought it in the first place. The only thing I don\'t like is that the white cover tray can easily be removed by a small child. In fact they can get their fingers pinched under it. I wish it attatched more securely.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is the best booster seat!  It is easy to tavel with, very light, and easy to clean.  I sometimes use it at home instead of his highchair.  My son seems to like using the booster seat better than sitting in the highchair.  He figured out that he can pull the the white insert tray off so I don\'t use that anymore but no big deal.  I have a friend who also has this seat and her son doesn\'t pull the tray off so I think it just depends on your kid.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I love this thing! It\'s inexpensive, east to use, easy to clean, portable, secure, and takes up very little space. It\'s the only high chair my child has ever used, and we use it at home, bring it to restaurants, to other peoples homes, and even brought it on vacation with us! She\'s 2 years old and still has room. I buy this for every new mom now. There\'s no need to spend $$$ on bulky high chairs that can tip over.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I was torn between buying a high chair or a booster seat so my 6 month old could sit with us during dinner. After reading other reviews, we went ahead and opted for the Fisher Price Healthy Care Deluxe Booster seat and I\'m really glad we did.  It\'s usually at our diningroom table but has been in restaurants, other people\'s homes, our livingroom floor, etc.  It is extremely easy to clean and portable. So glad we went this route.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This booster is perfect. It cleans easily, 6 month (now 9 month) baby loves it. This chair travels well but it also used everyday at grandma\'s house. I spent hours trying to be sure I bought something that baby would be comfortable in, but was also easy to clean and use. This chair is perfect! There is no cloth to need to wash, it wipes down easily. The best part, you can\'t beat the price!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Our twins are 20 months and we have used these since they could sit on their own.  We keep them in the car all the time to go out to eat.  You just can\'t guarentee that a restaurant will have clean high chairs available!  And those high chairs can\'t be placed at all tables due to size.  These boosters can go at any table.  The kids are getting big for them and we\'ll be sad to have to stop using them.  We don\'t use sippy cups so the cup holder isn\'t a problem-it holds quick straw cups.  Our kids never pull off the top tray-there\'s usually food on it!We can\'t say enough about how great these booster seats are!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I liked the color and the price was more than right.  My grandniece, however, at 7 months, was able to lift off the tray that sat in the base tray, making it unusable.  I now just let her sit with the tray base and feed her from a bowl in my hand.  I love the security of the seat and how easy it was to put onto my chair.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I\'ve used this great chair on the floor, in a chair and on the go. The hard back and seat are easy to wipe down; the straps are easy to wipe clean (or remove for a sink scrub if it\'s particularly pesky goo). The blue top is convenient for travelling, but spends most of the time in a cabinet out of the way. I\'ve sent the removable tray through the dishwasher once... it\'s so easy to clean in the sink with a sponge I rarely bother. I\'ve used a wet paper towel a few times. The attachment straps work well with my wooden chairs with slat backs. The baby straps hold the baby attach securely, keeping the center of gravity/weight in the chair, and the straps around the chair hold firm.I read concerns that this chair looked "hard" or uncomfortable. My baby doesn\'t seem to mind. He has a puffy diaper and sumo chubby thighs. They fit with the plastic\'s shape and don\'t seem crunched or too tight. After a big meal he might get sleepy and slouchy, but no more "uncomfortable looking" than in his car seat. He only really fusses if he drops a cereal bit and he can\'t pincer-grasp it up.In summary: Easy to clean, easy to adjust, easy to use (several times) every day.Caveats: Occasionally you should unattach it and clean the sides and bottom edge at the adjustable lifts because baby fingers hide food there. After the nooks and crannies of my last high chair, this is minimal. It\'s good practice to sanitize it with wipes every now and again, so be sure to check this area when you do and you\'re all set.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Our grand child comes often and we didn\'t want to invest in a high chair.  Found this item and ordered it right away!!  It puts our sweetie right up the the table with us,  Is safe and secure and it is portable so we can take it with us to any restaurant and know that she is safe and the booster seat is clean.  Oh, she loves it too!!  Another great Fisher-Price product!!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Our granddaughter is 8 months old and this makes taking her to restaurants really easy. More importantly is secures well and she is safe in it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought this for my son to use when we go out to eat. I absolutely love it! Easy to clean. Folds up easily. Light weight. A must have!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this because of the price compared to a full size High chair. I really love it. But i suggest covering your dining chair with a towel before installing the high chair because babies are very messy while eating.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We got this booster seat/high chair because we knew we were going to have only one child and didn\'t have the space to have a large high chair. It attaches easily to our kitchen chairs and I\'ve been putting our 5-month old daughter in it while I work in the kitchen for 2 months now. I love everything about this chair (easy to clean, height adjustable, sturdy) except for one thing (hence the 4 stars). It\'s hard to attach and detach the tray. It has three plastic "nubs" at different depths (so it can grow with your child) that you snap the tray over. You have to line them up well while attaching the tray. Once it\'s on it\'s on - it\'s not made for 1-hand removal. When she\'s having a fit and needs to get out immediately, I have a hard time detaching the tray and I worry about pulling too hard because I don\'t want to rock, or worse, tip the chair.We just started solid foods this weekend so it\'s getting easier to use as she gets used to sitting in it. I am glad that the white tray just snaps off so it\'s not messy to remove the blue tray. It would be the perfect product if the tray could just swing in and out for everyday use and completely remove for cleaning.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We have 2 twin boys who are 20 months old. They used to use an old wooden highchair at grandmas, but there was only one and it was falling apart. She bought these because they could work for my niece (3 years old) without the back and it could work with my 20 month olds as a highcahir. This chair is so convinent. The snap in tray is great, just like my Aquarium chair at home! It is also nice that it adjusts to the tray can rest on the table. I love that its VERY easy to fold and carry. My boys love sitting in it, and its SUPER easy to clean. We would buy one for restaurants, but we just use a floppy seat, less room and we need ALL the room with twins. I love this booster and its perfect for grandmas, houses with limited space, for going out to eat, or just instead of a highchair if you have multiple children! We love this chair, and would never use another one for grandmas.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Don\'t buy it thru Amazon.  I got it at Target for much cheaper.  Well worth it, however.  We have used it for a long time!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this booster a month ago when my 2-year-old needed to graduate from his highchair so his younger brother could have it.  I REALLY like this booster.  My son loves sitting at the table, and I love that he\'s still contained. :-)  With the seat on the lowest position, it can be pushed right under our table, even with the tray attached.  It folds very easily for travel, and the removable (and dishwasher-safe) tray insert makes for easy cleanup.  We traveled with this seat last week and ended up using it for my 9-month-old, and it worked nicely for him, as well.  The only fault I found is that the tray can be difficult to attach when my son is in the seat.  I would definitely buy this again, even to keep as an extra highchair at the grandparents\' house.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I needed a portable high chair for my grandson who was visiting for two weeks.  It was made well for the price and served the purpose very well. Was easy to attach to a kitchen chair and folds up for storage.  No sharp edges for little fingers to get caught on.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Other reviewers have touched on all of the features I love about this seat, so I will echo their raves. One thing I did want to reinforce though is that this seat is very versatile and will last you a long time. I didn\'t buy it for DS until he was 11 months old, but our nanny used it for her 5 month old baby. Now DS is 2 (36"+, nearly 30 pounds) and fits just as well in it as the 5 month old baby did, with or without the tray.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Not only do we use the booster seat, but when we have guests with toddlers, this seat comes in handy.  It\'s easy to clean and store.  The tray comes with a second layer for quick cleaning.  We liked it so much that we bought it as a baby gift for our niece!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have 3 of these, one at my sister\'s, one for the car and one for home. The only thing I didn\'t care for THIS one is that it doesn\'t have a hole in the back of the seat so you can use it as a handle. My other 2 which I had bought for my first son over 5 years ago has it.  I use these chairs for a long time! It made my older son stay put in restaurants!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is great for a grandparents house and to take to a restaurant. It is such a nice product and easy to assemble. The price is very reasonable as well. I\'m glad I got this product.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Doesn\'t take up room. my daughter is comfortable. Easy to clean.  convenient for traveling. We are very happy with it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: THIS WAS FOR MY GREAT GRANDDAUGHTER AND HAS AND STILL IS GOING A GREAT JOB.  VERY HAPPY WITH THIS ITEM.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This has been great for our baby so far.  It\'s sturdy, easy to put together, not hard to get tightly attached to the chair, and apparently pretty comfortable.  Our nine month old LOVES to sit in it!  He\'ll just drum happily on the tray until we bring the food over.We got this when our son was about 8 months old.  My husband and I were feeling very picky about high chairs whenever we looked at them in stores.  He kept favoring the really expensive ones for their sturdiness and comfort, while I favored the cheap ones because I know kids really don\'t use high chairs for that long of a time (and we might not have another baby).  I saw this on Amazon and thought the good reviews plus the chair\'s ability to "grow" with the kid by turning into a booster seat was GREAT. I mentioned it to my husband... and he said he wanted to see it in person first (meaning, we\'d hunt it down in a store)!  Well, I decided I was tired of our indecision and ordered it.  I told him we could return it at no cost if we didn\'t like it, so this was an ideal way to see it in person.  When he saw it strapped to a chair in our kitchen, he looked at it, jiggled it, moved pieces, put our son in it, and loved it!Problem solved.  :)

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This booster seat works great and is the second one I have bought for my second grandchild. I highly recommend it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We use this when we visit grandparents for meals and it is perfect.  It is easy to clean, very easy to transport and works great!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Love this booster! I got this when my daughter was 18 mth and wished I had it sooner. The size is perfect on the highest level and she is an average size baby. She loves sitting at the table with us. I have had a couple other booster/high chairs and this tray is by far the best. It can hold a child size plate which the other chairs could not do. Great product!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I hardly use the tray, but I do like that I can raise the seat up and down.  My kid loves it.  I wouldn\'t carry it around though, as it is bulky. Better than a high chair.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: When we started my son on jar food it was hard to handle him, the jar, the spoon and his roming hands.  Now it is so much easier to feed him. I love the fact that we can store it away when we are not using it, and my Sebastian loves sitting in it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I love love love this chair. I throw it over my shoulder with the convenient carrying strap it has, and it weighs close to nothing. I take it to every resturant and my baby has his own seat, not a sticky, germ infested resturant chair! He has his own tray to eat his Cherrios off of, and other good snacks. When he is done I can put the tray cover on and take it home and wash it. We take it to Grandmas and any of our friends homes and our little guy is all set to eat. We recently went to Jamaica and we set up the chair in our hotel room. When we were going out to eat we put this chair over the handles on the stroller with the carrying strap and we were set! You can also take off the tray and raise the seat up and they can join you you at the table.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought this for my son around the 6-month mark, and within the past month and a half, it\'s already been taken to restaurants and weekends away. It\'s a nice, sturdy design. My only tiny complaint is that the cover for the tray falls off easily. It doesn\'t seem to snap into place securely, which defeats the purpose. Overall, I still recommend it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have not even owned  this seat for a month and already you can see the strain on the plastic. The tray snaps on the seat and I am sure that it will be broken and unusable very soon. I am easy on it but the plastic is turning white where it snaps on- that should not be happening. It is a bad design so be smart and don\'t waste your money.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I love this thing.It\'s so easy to take with you wherever you go.  I\'ve found that most baby items seem to be a pain in the you-know-where when it comes to putting them together, installing them, or moving them.  This booster seat attaches to any chair with two clicks and is removed just as easily.Its removable tray has a cover so even if my dear baby makes a holy mess in a restaurant, I don\'t have to bother cleaning up - I just snap the lid on and off we go.It\'s easy to carry because the straps that connect it to the chair can be used as a carrying strap.  Or I usually hold it by the handle of the chair back.Plus, while at home, we leave it strapped onto one of the dining room table chairs - we don\'t use a high chair at all.  This takes up so much less space.  It\'s wonderful.In a world where so many things are so unnecessarily complicated, it\'s nice to have something so easy and reliable to use as this booster seat.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I actually use this booster for my 6 month old daughter. It does a great job of putting her at the table so that she can feel she is part of the family meals too. It was so much cheaper than the traditional high chair and way less bulky. Plus, I can take it with us when we travel. The trays are great. Super easy to wash. When I first started putting her in it, she wasn\'t able to sit up on her own but the trays and straps did a great job helping her to sit up unassisted. I would definitely recommend this product.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My mom bought one of these to take the place of a high chair when we had 2 8-9 month olds and a 3 year old at her house for christmas.  It is so comfortable, easy to use, attractive, and so easy to clean, that there is now one in our house and my brother and sister in law\'s house as well!  I have used ours for our 1 yr old every single time we go to a restaurant, ever since he got sick in Feb with a very painful virus which the doctor said one could catch in any public place.  I\'ve never been a panicky mom about cooties, but that was my limit.  With this chair, I can comfortable seat him at any restaurant and know he is safe and can both sit ina clean seat and eat his food off a clean tray.  I love that all parts of the tray go conveniently in the DW.  My son can be impatient, too, and both the seatbelt and the tray snapping on over his lap help keep him comfortably restrained. Not only do we use it for the little one in restaurants, but we use it for our almost-4 yr old to raise him to a comfortable height at our dining room table.  They are both big boys (90-95% in size), but both the 1 and 4 yr old fit comfortably.  It folds small enough that I can tuck it into my stroller basket to have on hand, and everyone loves how it all folds into a small package, with a convenient handle for carryign it.  Definitely a great thing to buy -- I would recommend it to a friend, or give it as a shower gift.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Pros: nice sturdy seat, plastic sections easy to clean. The colors are ok. protable. very handy. infants, toddlers find it comfortable. Cons: not sure how to clean the latches and fabric seat belts. not has cool looking as some of the other stylish items. Overall: good product. will use for baby number 3.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I used this for a few months until I bought my son a high chair. Its been great! My son finally grew out of it (he\'s a fast grower). It totally got the job done and really helped me when I didn\'t have enough room for a real high chair. Its cleans easily! Totally sturdy and you can take it anywhere! I LOVE THIS PRODUCT!! It was a life saver and when I need to ever use it for my next child I know it will be right there waiting! I highly recommend this product!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This booster seat is great. It straps onto the chair so even when your child is antsy, the seat will not fall off the chair and your child will not get hurt!! I have wood chairs and that was one of my biggest concerns. This also works great for when you\'re eating snacks on the couch, it gives your child a little table to have with them anywhere!! It\'s dishwasher safe and easy to close up and take with you on a trip. It even has a strap (double use from securing to the chair) that allows it to be carried over the shoulder. Easy to clean even the straps are removable and washable!! Item is available at Target or Walmart for about $25!! Great price also!!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this inexpensive chair for use at my parents\' house and I wish this is the one I would have gotten for myself instead of the more expensive one I have. This chair is a great space saver, it\'s an awesome little high chair. LOVE it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Fabulous way to feed my son (now 13 months) at the table without a bulky, messy, expensive high chair. The booster fits securely on our kitchen chair at a great height and pulls up to the table nicely. Very easy to clean. My old traditional high chair was a hot mess to clean. Waaaaay too many nooks & crannies for something met to feed a baby! Wish I\'d had this for my oldest!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Have been using this chair for three weeks now and love it. My son is 10 months old and fits great in this chair. It also works great to place him in while I cook, he can watch whats going on. Its really easy to use and clean. The belts come off the chair to wash and the trays fit easily in the dishwasher.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this recently for my 20 month-old daughter who showed signs that she was ready to sit at the \'big\' table with us. She absolutely loves sitting in this seat! I use it with the tray and sometimes I remove the tray and pull it up to the table. I like the fact that the height can be adjusted as the baby grows. It\'s also very easy to clean after meals. We plan to take it with us to restaurants (when we start eating out again :)! I wish we had bought this from the beginning instead of buying a high-chair...

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My Great Granddaughter is so happy to be able to leave her highchair and now sit at the table with Mommy and Daddy.  Every time we visit she thanks us for this chair.  It is well made and easily attached to chair.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I highly recommend this seat. We gave our traditional high chair away when our son was6-months-old. He is now over 1-year-old. We take the seat with us on vacations, dining out, and visits to the grandparents\' homes. Easy to clean, easy to store. Wonderful product!!!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This product is self explanatory, so no need for an extensive review. So I\'ll just mention a few things that I was pondering about prior to buying.1.) Does the tray swing with a hinge?No, you have to remove it completely, or use it. It basically clips in.2.) Can you adjust the height of the seat while your child is sitting on it?No, the adjustment is made on the underside. You\'ll have to flip the booster over to play with some latches. Very easy though.3.) Can you remove the back support?Yes.For $25, everything is acceptable. And we should have bought this sooner. We use our highchair in two different rooms in the house, one of which is the dining room. No need to lug the high chair around anymore.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My booster seat has been used by 4 different children, and still looks like new.Used daily for the past 5 years, and still like new.  Very good quality, well made, I would recommend this product to anyone wanting a "portable high chair".

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought two of these for our church and love them.  The trays go through our commercial dishwasher and give peace of mind regarding sanitation for our little ones.  The seats fit securely on our padded chairs and put the little ones at just the right height to either eat from the tray or right up to the table.  Best of all, the seat itself is smooth and cleans up easily.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This is great for my grandbabies. Not sure how long they will be able to use it. Time will tell. Seems a little small from seat to tray. ?  Love the different options of trays.  I recommend this booster seat.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I bought this for my one year old Granddaughter.  It worked great, was sturdy, and was easily strapped securely to a dining room chair.  Granddaughter also used it on the floor as a play chair.  I recommend it highly.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Best invention for baby-to-3-year-old ever!  Traditional high chair is not necessary!  This chair straps safely to ordinary adult dining chair and holds baby safely and snugly for easy feeding.  Without the trays, it is an excellent booster seat for your toddler.  I highly recommend this as the #1 necessity for new parents.  It\'s portable and easy to take to restaurants and Grandma\'s house.  I can\'t say enough good things about this great product.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Bought two of these for twin grand babies. Easy to clean and use , only drawback is the twins are starting to get to big for any of their chairs.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have two of these and they are great.Pros:- Easy to clean (you may decide you don\'t even need the top two trays like me)- Works with infants (as soon as they can sit up really) through older toddlers- Adjustable height and straps for attaching to other chairs and sitting at other tables (like when you have to take it to grandma\'s house)Cons:- The only con I can think of is on the second one we bought there was some plastic flashing that needed to be trimmed a bit for the main tray to attach more easily to the chair.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This was an excellent buy!  My 6 month old sat right in it and LOVED it, she felt like a grown up joining us at meal times.  It\'s adjustable, easy to feed her from, easy to wash (dishwasher safe trays), easy to fold and take with you to restaurants etc!  My best friend saw mine and is now wishing she got one of these instead of her much more expensive high chair!!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We bought this chair when our son started on solids.  Every high chair we looked at was either flimsy, clunky, too hard to clean, or way too expensive - so we opted for this booster seat as a compromise.  If it didn\'t work as a high chair, at least we have a portable seat when we needed it and we\'re only out $25!  So far it\'s worked great!  Our son is 10 months old and this is still his only high chair.I love it because it\'s a great multi-tasker (Alton Brown would be so proud!)  Since it attaches to any chair with a back you can take it anywhere - restaurants, grandma\'s house.  And at home it doesn\'t take up half of your kitchen!  But don\'t forget that it\'s only as stable as the chair it\'s attached to!I only have one complaint and that\'s the removable tray.  Once your child figures out how to take it off - forget about it!  The front (closest to the child) is the only part that snaps on, so all they have to do is reach over and grab the opposing side and then the whole thing comes off!  But this is a pretty minor inconvenience - the rest of the tray is very easy to clean.  The top to ours is in a closet and I haven\'t missed it!Another tip - make sure to put something underneath the booster seat if you can.  A towel goes a long way toward keeping your chairs from getting completely covered in baby food!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I think my biggest issue with this chair is that my baby is very uncomfortable in it. He would scream every time I tried to put him in it. I ended up buying a regular high chair with a padded seat and he has no problem sitting in it (though he has no problem sitting in hard restaurant high chairs). He\'s 6 months old now, so perhaps when he\'s older he\'ll like it more. The only advantages of the fisher price booster seat are that it\'s very portable, inexpensive, and might be good for people with don\'t have an extra 2 feet of space for a high chair. But it doesn\'t matter how portable or inexpensive it is if your baby hates it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I love this seat.  I use it whenever we are going somewhere that I know doesn\'t have a highchair.  Grandma bought one of these instead of a traditional highchair.  I also use it whenever another child will be eatting at my house, and my daughter is in the highchair.  I purchased this over a year ago, and my 18 mo old still fits in it.  My only complaint is that she very quickly learned how to pop the tray insert out of the tray, and on several occasions, dumped it\'s contents all over the place.  But now I just use the tray itself, and don\'t bother with the removable insert.  This seat fits on a regualar chair, and it will slide under most of the tables I\'ve tried it with, (With the tray off.)  Everywhere I take this seat, I get people commenting on the practicallity of it, and many ask where they can purchase one!This is a good investment. - posted January 2005Added December 2006My daughter is now 3 1/2, and is sitting in a regular chair.  Her 1 year old little brother is now using this booster seat.  It has held up great, and has little sign of wear.  The tray insert is never used at our house, as his little fingers can easily pry it off and fling it and his dinner across the room.  But the blue bottom tray is easy to wipe clean, and even fits in my dishwasher!  This product has stood the test of time, and two toddlers!  It is well worth the investment, and gets my stamp of approval.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This chair is great.  I am so glad I didn\'t waste money and space by buying a stand-alone highchair.  My nine-month-old loves to sit in it.  We have it on the second height setting right now and it slides nicely under our table. The only criticism I have is that the extra tray cover doesn\'t really seem necessary.  My baby just pulls it off and plays with it.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Pros----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------* Nice, lightweight,easy to put together* Easy clean/washed it in dishwasher with no problem. unlike the big chair* Love the multiple trays/adjustable seat* straps for safety.* Baby can join us on dining table and he looks around and likes being the part of conversation* cost effective in terms of time/effort saved in cleaning, plus grows with the babyCon-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The straps are short and baby can put \'em in his mouth. That is the only downside we found so far.but actually that is really not big of a deal because we twirl it around so that no loose ends are hanging.Also--------You can also buy the replacement tray/parts/toy attachments from [...]but do check the model number of seat you have. Certain parts only match with certain models. They have good customer service reps who answer your questions well.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: not having purchased a booster seat before, was impressed with the innovative features (removable tray, height adjustment) of the seat.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I have two- one at my house and one at my sister\'s house- works great, easy to use, easy to transport if needed.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: We mostly eat dinner at our island. We use this attached to a bar stool with a back. Its soooo much better than a highchair-and no more floor space is taken up than it ever is-because it is attached to the chair. This is my second fisher-price detachable seat.WHAT I LOVE:- It has a detachable tray (easy to clean)-It has food plate that attaches to detachable tray. (even easier to clean)-The detachable tray has a LID-so, if they don\'t finish eating -you can just put the lid on the detachable tray and throw it in the fridge.-the whole thing breaks down enough to put in the dishwasher.-the straps are adjustable-my baby is off the charts height/weight-so where the straps not adjustable(like so many are) we couldn\'t use it.-It inexpensive enough that if it looks horrible in a year or so-buying a new one isn\'t that big of a deal.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My 3 year old son loves being able to sit at the table in a chair and I love not having to lift him into his highchair.  The red parts of this chair are actually a beautiful red, not burgundy as the picture portrays.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: After reading some of the 800+ reviews, almost entirely in favor of this seat, we bought it for our then 3-month old, knowing it might be a little while before he could really sit up in it well.  To our surprise, he did great!  At first, he could sit in it for a few minutes before he\'d start to list to one side.  Now, he\'s almost 6 months old and he\'s eating solid foods a few times a week.  This chair is PERFECT.  He can sit in it just fine.  You can use the tray or slide the baby up to the table, which is what we usually do.  The tray does fit great into the dishwasher.  The chair is super easy to clean and it\'ll be nice later on to have a portable high chair for him.  I\'m so glad we didn\'t spend a ton of money on a chair that wouldn\'t do anything more than what this one does so well...support your child in a safe place while they learn to eat.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: It\'s very secure and does a great job of keeping my toddler seated during mealtime. The trays are dishwasher safe which is always a plus. The only thing is that my 1 year old figured out very quickly how to remove the inner tray which has become a toy for her. Luckily she hasn\'t figured out how to remove the main tray.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My granddaughter really enjoyed using this booster seat. It was easy to use and the extra top was a bonus. She has now grown out of it and the seat is waiting for the next granddaughter to grow into.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Love this booster seat. We have tried several different seats and this by far has been the best. Straps perfectly to every seat we have used it on, has removable back, 2 trays, height adjutment, adjustable straps, 3pt harness, folds comatc for travel or storage and also seems to be the most comfy to sit in for our 2 boys. We will also be using this same seat for our 3rd boy when the time comes. Worth every penny!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Love this chair. Started my 4 month old in it. He loves it. It\'s nice how it\'s adjustable w age so he\'ll be using it for many more months. Also, very durable and easy to clean. A def steal for the price. Buy it, you will enjoy.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I\'m not going to write a very long review because there are already over 700 hundred reviews for this product. Based on those reviews I bought this chair. My 11 month old daughter was in it for less than 5 minutes when she pulled the top tray right off, spilling the food onto the floor. I replaced it and she promptly did it again. I would suggest holding on to your receipt, if your child figures out the tray trick then return the chair, if not-- enjoy!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: My baby girl loves it and me too. I can take it everywhere, it is super secure and easy to clean

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: my little boy loves this seat i take this every war i go it work at the park and at the house

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: This highchair is a good value and very cute in red and cream. It\'s perfect for our student budget and apartment. We love it!

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: Have had no problems with this product. It comes apart easy and can be thrown in the dishwasher.  Easy to use & very durable.

name: Fisher-Price Booster Seat, Blue/Green/Gray
review: I didn\'t receive a high chair from my registry, so I decided to wait until my baby was six months old to buy a high chair.  My sister-in-law brought one of these on a family vacation, and I thought it was brilliant.  I don\'t have a lot of space, so I was looking for a space saving high chair anyway.  This one is actually portable, you can bring it to restaurants and everything!  And it\'s only $30?
